exports.description: Where the avatar's image is in its life.

exports.name: formatProgressValue
exports.description:
The value as text: `""` without a value; a percentage (`value / 100`, so 50 reads "50%") without
`format`; otherwise `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, format)` of the value itself.
exports.signature: (value: number | null | undefined, locale: Intl.LocalesArgument, format: Intl.NumberFormatOptions | undefined) => string

exports.name: progressIndicatorPercent
exports.description: The width of a fill in percent, or `null` when there is no finite value (indeterminate: nothing to size).
exports.signature: (value: number | null | undefined, min: number, max: number) => number | null

exports.name: progressStatus
exports.description: The status for `value` (`null` or not a finite number means indeterminate) against `max`.
exports.signature: (value: number | null | undefined, max: number) => ProgressStatus

exports.name: progressValueText
exports.description: The default `aria-valuetext`: the formatted value (or `value%` when that is empty), `indeterminate progress` without a value.
exports.signature: (formattedValue: string | null, value: number | null | undefined) => string

exports.name: valueToPercent
exports.description: Where `value` sits between `min` and `max`, in percent (not clamped, like the DOM attributes it feeds).
exports.signature: (value: number, min: number, max: number) => number

exports.name: ProgressStatus
exports.description: A bar with no value is `indeterminate`, one at its maximum is `complete`, anything else `progressing`.

exports.name: acceptsDismissal
exports.description:
Does this gesture dismiss? Escape always reaches the layer's `onOpenChange`; an outside press and a
focus-out are refused when the host set `disablePointerDismissal` (an alert dialog always does). Whether the
layer is the one the gesture belongs to is the dismiss-layer model's decision, made before this one.

exports.name: defaultInitialFocus
exports.description:
The default initial focus of a dialog: by touch the popup itself (so the on-screen keyboard does not pop up
for a first text field), otherwise its first tab stop.

exports.name: layerBehavior
exports.description:
The table: `true` traps, locks, hides and shields; `"trap-focus"` only traps; `false` does none of it and
lets focus leave (which dismisses). Pinned by `__tests__/dialog.test.ts`.

exports.name: outsidePressDismisses
exports.description:
Which presses outside a layer dismiss it. A NON-modal layer (`modal` false): every one. A modal layer: only a
press on its own backdrop or shield, or on something that holds the popup (the viewport, the page body).
A press on anything else that is not in the popup (a menu, a popover or a toast that was opened from inside
the dialog and lives in a portal of its own) is that thing's business, never a dismissal of the dialog: inside by the React tree, or by being a node added to the body while the dialog was open.

exports.name: LayerBehavior
exports.description: What an open layer does to the rest of the page and to focus, per `modal`.

exports.name: ModalMode
exports.description: `modal` as the host writes it: `true` (default), `false`, or `"trap-focus"` (trapped, but the page stays scrollable and clickable).

exports.name: OutsidePressFacts
exports.description: What is known about the element a press landed on, for `outsidePressDismisses`.

exports.name: MAX_RELEASE_VELOCITY_AGE_MS
exports.description: A last drag sample older than this (ms) at release means the pointer stopped: the release speed is 0.

exports.name: MAX_SNAP_VELOCITY
exports.description: Speeds above this are treated as this when projecting a snap release.

exports.name: MAX_SWIPE_RELEASE_DURATION_MS
exports.description: Release animation: the longest exit duration in ms.

exports.name: MAX_SWIPE_RELEASE_SCALAR
exports.description: Release animation: the largest `--drawer-swipe-strength` scalar (the slowest exit).

exports.name: MAX_SWIPE_RELEASE_VELOCITY
exports.description: Release animation: the top of the speed range (px per ms); faster releases count as this.

exports.name: MIN_DRAG_THRESHOLD
exports.description: A press must move this far (px) before it counts as a drag at all.

exports.name: MIN_RELEASE_VELOCITY_DURATION_MS
exports.description: And over at least this long between two drag samples (ms).

exports.name: MIN_SWIPE_RELEASE_DURATION_MS
exports.description: Release animation: duration range in ms, and the range of the 0.1 to 1 scalar CSS reads as `--drawer-swipe-strength`.

exports.name: MIN_SWIPE_RELEASE_SCALAR
exports.description: Release animation: the smallest `--drawer-swipe-strength` scalar (the fastest exit).

exports.name: MIN_SWIPE_RELEASE_VELOCITY
exports.description: Release animation: speed range (px per ms) the exit duration is derived from.

exports.name: MIN_VELOCITY_DURATION_MS
exports.description: Speed is measured over at least this long a stretch of the whole gesture (ms), so a one-frame flick is not infinite.

exports.name: SNAP_VELOCITY_MULTIPLIER
exports.description: Converts a snap release's speed (px per ms) to px of extra travel.

exports.name: SNAP_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD
exports.description: With snap points, a release at or above this speed moves toward the next point.

exports.name: SWIPE_FAST_VELOCITY
exports.description: A release at or above this speed (px per ms) in the dismiss direction closes, however short the drag.

exports.name: SWIPE_MIN_THRESHOLD
exports.description: Movement under this many px never counts as a dismissal, whatever the popup's size.

exports.name: SWIPE_REVERSE_CANCEL_THRESHOLD
exports.description: A change of mind: moving back this many px from the furthest point cancels a single-direction swipe.

exports.name: allowedDirections
exports.description: The allowed-directions record for a list of directions.

exports.name: candidateDirection
exports.description:
The direction a movement points to, given the axis lock (when the gesture accepts both axes). `undefined`
for no movement on the locked axis, and for no movement at all (the first move of a gesture re-bases its start, so its delta is 0: reading that as `left` would
commit a toast that accepts both `left` and `right` to the wrong one; Base UI's has this quirk).
exports.signature: (deltaX: number, deltaY: number, lock: "horizontal" | "vertical" | null) => SwipeDirection | undefined

exports.name: canSwipeFromScrollEdge
exports.description: A move that began on a scroll container hands over to the swipe when it goes toward dismissal AND the container is at that edge.
exports.signature: (metrics: SwipeScrollMetrics, axis: "vertical" | "horizontal", direction: SwipeDirection, delta: number) => boolean

exports.name: canSwipeFromScrollEdgeOnPendingMove
exports.description: The pending-move variant: whether a swipe may begin from a scroll container's edge given the first moves (`null` when neither axis moved).
exports.signature: (scroll: { readonly vertical: SwipeScrollMetrics; readonly horizontal: SwipeScrollMetrics; }, deltaX: number, deltaY: number, allowed: AllowedDirections) => boolean | null

exports.name: createVelocityTracker
exports.description: Creates a velocity tracker with no samples.

exports.name: dampSwipeDelta
exports.description: Movement away from every allowed direction is damped to a square root, so the popup resists instead of following the pointer.
exports.signature: (deltaX: number, deltaY: number, allowed: AllowedDirections) => { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; }

exports.name: decideSnapRelease
exports.description:
What a release does on a drawer with snap points. The drag target is the current offset plus the drag
(clamped to the popup); a fast release projects further (`SNAP_VELOCITY_MULTIPLIER` px per px/ms). The
result is the nearest point, or CLOSE when the fully hidden position (offset = popup height) is nearer than
any point or the fling was fast and downward. In sequential mode a fast fling past the adjacent point
stops at it, and a fast fling past the lowest point closes.

exports.name: dismissFromStartEdge
exports.description:
Whether the drawer is dismissed from the START edge of a scroll container (scrolled to its top for a
`down` drawer, to its left for a `right` one) or from its END edge; `null` when the swipe direction is
not on this axis, so the container always scrolls.

exports.name: findClosestSnapPoint
exports.description: The point whose height is nearest `height` (the first on a tie), or null for none.
exports.signature: (height: number, points: readonly ResolvedSnapPoint[]) => ResolvedSnapPoint | null

exports.name: gestureVelocity
exports.description: Speed (px per ms) over the whole gesture, with a floor on the duration so a quick flick is finite.
exports.signature: (deltaX: number, deltaY: number, durationMs: number) => { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; }

exports.name: isAtSwipeStartEdge
exports.description: A press that begins on a scroll container may start a swipe only when the container sits at the edge the swipe starts from.

exports.name: isDirectionAllowed
exports.description: Whether the gesture accepts `direction`.

exports.name: isHorizontalDirection
exports.description: Whether `direction` is on the horizontal axis (`left` or `right`).

exports.name: lockAxis
exports.description: Which axis a gesture on a drawer that accepts both locks to, from the first real movement.

exports.name: releaseStrength
exports.description:
The 0.1 to 1 scalar a dismissing release writes as `--drawer-swipe-strength`: a fast flick gets a short
exit, a slow drag past the threshold a long one. `null` when the release has no outward speed to speak of
(CSS then keeps its default of 1).

exports.name: resolveActiveSnapPoint
exports.description:
The resolved point the active snap point stands for: the exact match, else the nearest point to where the
value resolves (a controlled value that is not in the list), else nothing (`null` active: closed).
exports.signature: (active: SnapPointValue | null | undefined, points: readonly ResolvedSnapPoint[], measure: SnapMeasure) => ResolvedSnapPoint | undefined

exports.name: resolveSnapPoints
exports.description:
Every snap point as a height and an offset, clamped to what the popup can show. Points that land within a
px of another resolve to one (the LAST of them wins), and an unreadable point is dropped. Empty until the
viewport and the popup have a size.
exports.signature: (snapPoints: readonly SnapPointValue[] | undefined, measure: SnapMeasure) => readonly ResolvedSnapPoint[]

exports.name: resolveSnapPointValue
exports.description: A snap point in px, or `null` when it cannot be read (unknown unit, not finite, no viewport).
exports.signature: (snapPoint: SnapPointValue, viewportHeight: number, rootFontSize: number) => number | null

exports.name: shouldDismissOnRelease
exports.description:
A drawer without snap points: does this release dismiss it? Yes when it moved toward the edge and either
left fast (average speed at least `SWIPE_FAST_VELOCITY`) or went past half of its size. Moving away from
the edge, or no committed direction, never does.
exports.signature: ({ direction, deltaX, deltaY, velocityX, velocityY, size }: ReleaseInput) => boolean

exports.name: shouldPreserveCrossAxisScroll
exports.description:
A touch that starts on a drawer containing a cross-axis scroller (a horizontal carousel in a bottom
drawer) keeps its native scroll when the gesture is mostly across: at least 6 px across and more than 2 px
further across than along.

exports.name: snapPointRange
exports.description: Offsets span between the highest point and the next one down: swipe progress runs 0 to 1 over this range.
exports.signature: (points: readonly ResolvedSnapPoint[]) => { readonly minOffset: number; readonly range: number; } | null

exports.name: swipeDismissThreshold
exports.description: The dismiss distance for a popup of `size` px along the swipe axis: half of it, never under the minimum.

exports.name: swipeDisplacement
exports.description: How far the pointer moved toward `direction`: positive is toward it, negative away.
exports.signature: (direction: SwipeDirection | undefined, deltaX: number, deltaY: number) => number

exports.name: swipeProgress
exports.description: Swipe progress 0 to 1: how far toward the edge, as a share of the popup's size (scaled by its current scale).
exports.signature: (displacement: number, size: number, scale?: number) => number

exports.name: AllowedDirections
exports.description: Which directions a gesture accepts.

exports.name: DragSample
exports.description: One drag position (px offset from the start) at `time` (ms).

exports.name: ReleaseInput
exports.description: What `shouldDismissOnRelease` needs: the gesture's direction, travel, average speed and the popup's size.

exports.name: ReleaseStrengthInput
exports.description: What `releaseStrength` needs: the gesture's direction, travel and speeds, the popup's size and the snap point offset.

exports.name: ResolvedSnapPoint
exports.description: A snap point resolved against the viewport and the popup: its height and its offset.

exports.name: SwipeScrollMetrics
exports.description: Scroll position of a scroll container along one axis: `offset` is scrollTop or scrollLeft, `max` the furthest it goes.

exports.name: SnapMeasure
exports.description: The sizes snap points resolve against, in px.

exports.name: SnapPointValue
exports.description: A snap point as the host writes it: 0 to 1 is a share of the viewport height, above 1 is px, `"320px"` and `"20rem"` are lengths.

exports.name: SnapRelease
exports.description: What a release on a drawer with snap points does: close, settle on a point, or nothing.

exports.name: SnapReleaseInput
exports.description: What `decideSnapRelease` needs: the drawer's direction, the vertical travel and speeds, the resolved points and where the drawer sits.

exports.name: SwipeDirection
exports.description: The direction a drawer is dismissed in: the edge it slides off toward.

exports.name: VelocityTracker
exports.description: Tracks drag samples to give the pointer's speed at release.

exports.name: createDrawerProviderStore
exports.description: Creates the store a `Drawer.Provider` holds.

exports.name: DrawerProviderStore
exports.description: Which drawers under a `Drawer.Provider` are open, so the page behind can indent while any is.

exports.name: DrawerVisualState
exports.description: What the frontmost swipe looks like from outside the drawer.

props.name: swipeProgress
props.description: 0 (at rest) to 1 (fully swiped away).

props.name: frontmostHeight
props.description: The height in px of the frontmost drawer while it swipes, else 0.

exports.name: DrawerVisualStore
exports.description: The live visual state of the frontmost swipe: a store `Drawer.Indent` reads with `useSyncExternalStore`.

exports.name: oppositeSwipeDirection
exports.description: The opposite direction: the drawer dismisses toward `down`, so its swipe area opens it toward `up`.

exports.name: shouldOpenOnRelease
exports.description: Does a release open the drawer? `displacement` is the drag toward the opening direction, `velocity` the release speed toward it (px per ms).
exports.signature: (input: { readonly displacement: number; readonly velocity: number; readonly threshold: number; readonly direction: SwipeDirection | undefined; readonly openDirection: SwipeDirection; }) => boolean

exports.name: swipeOpenPosition
exports.description:
The popup's position for a drag of `displacement` px toward the opening direction. The popup starts `closedOffset` px away from
its place (its own size, or less when an enter transform leaves it partway) and comes in with the finger; beyond its place the drag
is damped. `dismissDirection` is the edge it comes from (the drawer's own `swipeDirection`).
exports.signature: (input: { readonly displacement: number; readonly closedOffset: number; readonly dismissDirection: SwipeDirection; }) => SwipeOpenPosition

exports.name: swipeOpenThreshold
exports.description: The drag distance that opens a drawer `popupSize` px long along the swipe axis (`null`: not known).

exports.name: SWIPE_OPEN_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD
exports.description: The distance to pass when the popup's size is unknown (it is not mounted yet).

exports.name: SWIPE_OPEN_RATIO
exports.description: The drag must reach this share of the popup's size for a slow release to open it.

exports.name: SWIPE_OPEN_START_DISTANCE
exports.description: The drawer starts to open once the drag moved this far (px) toward its edge.

exports.name: SWIPE_OPEN_VELOCITY
exports.description: A release at or above this speed (px per ms) toward the open direction opens, however short the drag.

exports.name: SwipeOpenPosition
exports.description: Where the popup is while it is dragged in: how far it still has to travel and the progress that follows.

exports.name: ANCHORED_ALIGNS
exports.description: Alignment along the anchor's edge; `center` is the absence of an alignment suffix in a placement.

exports.name: ANCHORED_PLACEMENTS
exports.description: All 12 placements, side-major (the order of `ANCHORED_SIDES`, then center, start, end).

exports.name: ANCHORED_SIDES
exports.description: The four physical sides of an anchor a popup can sit on.

exports.name: alignOf
exports.description: The alignment of a placement; `center` when it has none.

exports.name: intersectRects
exports.description: Both rectangles' overlap; a zero-size rectangle at the first one's origin when they do not overlap.

exports.name: logicalSide
exports.description: The side of a rendered placement as `data-side` reports it: `inline-start` / `inline-end` when the caller asked logically.
exports.signature: (requested: AnchoredSideRequest, rendered: AnchoredSide, rtl: boolean) => AnchoredSideRequest

exports.name: oppositePlacement
exports.description: The placement on the opposite side with the same alignment (`top-start` → `bottom-start`).

exports.name: overflowOf
exports.description: How far `rect` crosses each edge of `boundary`: positive = overflowing by that many pixels, negative = room left, 0 = flush. `padding` shrinks the boundary.
exports.signature: (rect: PlacementRect, boundary: PlacementRect, padding: PlacementPadding) => PlacementPadding

exports.name: physicalSide
exports.description: The physical side a request means in the given writing direction.

exports.name: placementOf
exports.description: The placement for a side and alignment.

exports.name: sideOf
exports.description: The side of a placement.

exports.name: toPadding
exports.description: A number or a partial per-edge padding as a full per-edge padding.
exports.signature: (padding: number | Partial<PlacementPadding> | undefined, fallback?: number) => PlacementPadding

exports.name: AnchoredAlign
exports.description: One of `ANCHORED_ALIGNS`: where the popup lines up along the anchor's edge.

exports.name: AnchoredPlacement
exports.description: One of the 12 placements: a side, optionally followed by `-start` or `-end` (`bottom`, `bottom-start`, `left-end`).

exports.name: AnchoredSide
exports.description: One of `ANCHORED_SIDES`: the side of the anchor the popup sits on.

exports.name: AnchoredSideRequest
exports.description: A side as a caller may ask for it: physical, or logical (`inline-start` / `inline-end` follow the writing direction).

exports.name: PlacementPadding
exports.description: Space kept between the popup and each edge of the collision rectangle.

exports.name: PlacementRect
exports.description: A rectangle in any one coordinate space (viewport pixels, or relative to a containing block).

exports.name: PlacementSize
exports.description: A width and a height, in px.

exports.name: POPUP_PLACEMENTS
exports.description: Where the popup goes relative to its anchor.

exports.name: placePopup
exports.description: The default positioner: flips above when there is no room below, clamps to the viewport edges, and opens submenus to the right (or left when that does not fit).

exports.name: AnchorRect
exports.description: The anchor's box in viewport pixels (the fields of a `DOMRect` the maths reads).

exports.name: PlacedPopup
exports.description: The answer of a positioner: the popup's fixed top-left and the height it may grow to.

exports.name: PlacementRequest
exports.description: What a positioner is asked: the anchor, the popup's natural size, the viewport and the wanted placement.

exports.name: PopupPlacement
exports.description: One of `POPUP_PLACEMENTS`: where the small placer puts a popup relative to its anchor.

exports.name: PopupPoint
exports.description: A point anchor (a context menu at the pointer).

exports.name: PopupPositioner
exports.description: The placement seam: our default is `placePopup`; any function of this shape replaces it.

exports.name: adaptiveOriginOf
exports.description:
Base UI's `adaptiveOrigin` middleware: for a popup on the `left` side the horizontal coordinate becomes the distance from the offset
parent's right edge, for a popup on the `top` side the vertical one the distance from its bottom edge. A popup that changes size
(a viewport morphing between two triggers' content) then keeps its edge that faces the anchor in place and grows away from it.
exports.signature: (x: number, y: number, placement: AnchoredPlacement, floating: PlacementSize, offsetParent: PlacementSize) => AdaptiveOrigin

exports.name: computeAnchoredPosition
exports.description:
Computes the popup's position. Pure: the same options always give the same result.

Matches Base UI 1.4.1's `useAnchorPositioning` configured with `positionMethod: "absolute"` and the
default `collisionAvoidance`. `lockedSide` is its `lazyFlip` (the side the last placement settled on becomes the starting
placement) and `adaptiveOrigin` its `adaptiveOrigin` middleware; both default to off.

exports.name: defaultOrigin
exports.description: `adaptiveOrigin` off: the coordinates as they are, from the top-left corner.

exports.name: AdaptiveOrigin
exports.description: The CSS properties a popup's coordinates are written to, and the values for them.

exports.name: AnchoredArrowPosition
exports.description: The arrow's offset along the alignment axis; only the axis of the rendered placement is set.

exports.name: AnchoredArrowSize
exports.description: The arrow's box; omit for a popup without one.

exports.name: AnchoredOffsetData
exports.description: What a function-valued `sideOffset` / `alignOffset` is told about the placement it is offsetting.

exports.name: AnchoredPositionOptions
exports.description: What `computeAnchoredPosition` needs: the anchor and popup boxes, the placement, offsets, collision rules and an optional arrow.

exports.name: AnchoredPositionResult
exports.description: Where `computeAnchoredPosition` puts the popup: its corner, the placement it settled on, and the arrow and size data.

exports.name: CollisionAvoidance
exports.description: How `computeAnchoredPosition` keeps the popup inside the collision rectangle, per axis.

exports.name: CollisionAvoidanceMode
exports.description: How the popup reacts to leaving the collision rectangle on the side axis or the alignment axis.

exports.name: createPopupHandleStore
exports.description: Creates an empty popup handle store: closed, no triggers, no binding.
exports.signature: <Payload = unknown, Trigger = unknown, Host = unknown>() => PopupHandleStore<Payload, Trigger, Host>

exports.name: PopupBinding
exports.description: What a Root attaches: the value detached triggers read, and how a request to open or close is applied.

exports.name: PopupHandleSnapshot
exports.description: What a popup handle store holds at one moment: a new object on every change, so it is a stable snapshot for subscribers.

exports.name: PopupHandleStore
exports.description: The store behind a popup handle: the triggers several parts register, the one the popup is attached to, its payload and its open state.

exports.name: PopupPayloadBox
exports.description: A payload boxed so "the active trigger has `undefined` as its payload" is distinguishable from "no payload yet".

exports.name: PopupTriggerRecord
exports.description: One registered trigger.

exports.name: NAVIGATION_MENU_CLOSE_DELAY
exports.description: How long (ms) after the pointer leaves the menu closes (Base UI's default).

exports.name: NAVIGATION_MENU_DELAY
exports.description: The pointer rests this long over a trigger before it opens a closed menu, and leaving closes after this long (Base UI's defaults, ms).

exports.name: navigationActivationDirection
exports.description:
The direction the menu moved when the active trigger changed from `from` to `to`: in a horizontal menu `right` when the new trigger is
further right and `left` when further left, in a vertical one `down` and `up`. `null` when the triggers sit at the same place along the
menu's axis (a menu whose triggers wrap onto a second row keeps the direction it had).
exports.signature: (from: NavigationBox, to: NavigationBox, orientation: NavigationMenuOrientation) => NavigationActivationDirection | null

exports.name: navigationContentSide
exports.description: The physical side of its trigger that content sits on, from the two boxes' centres (the longer axis of the difference wins; a tie is horizontal).

exports.name: navigationOpenKey
exports.description:
The key that opens a trigger's content and moves into it: ArrowDown in a horizontal menu, the arrow that points toward the inline end in a
vertical one (ArrowRight, mirrored in right to left text; Base UI's is always ArrowRight).

exports.name: navigationReturnsFocus
exports.description:
Whether a close gives focus back to the trigger (when focus is inside the content or lost to the body): Escape, a pressed link and a
pressed trigger do. A hover, an outside press and focus moving away on its own do not (focus is somewhere the user put it).

exports.name: NavigationActivationDirection
exports.description: The direction the menu moved when its active trigger changed: toward the right, left, down or up (Base UI's `data-activation-direction`).

exports.name: NavigationBox
exports.description: The part of a rectangle the decisions read.

exports.name: NavigationMenuOrientation
exports.description: Which way the navigation menu's triggers are laid out, and so which arrow keys move between them.

exports.name: ACTIVATION_DIRECTION_TOLERANCE
exports.description: An offset smaller than this (px) on an axis counts as no movement on it, as Base UI's.

exports.name: activationDirection
exports.description: The `data-activation-direction` value for a move of `offset`: `"right down"`, `"left "`, `" up"`, or `undefined` when there is no move to describe.

exports.name: nextContentKeyMemory
exports.description: Steps the bookkeeping in `ContentKeyMemory`: returns the new memory and whether the content key must change (`bump`).
exports.signature: (previous: ContentKeyMemory, triggerId: string | null, payload: unknown) => { readonly memory: ContentKeyMemory; readonly bump: boolean; }

exports.name: relativeOffset
exports.description: How far the centre of `to` is from the centre of `from`.

exports.name: ContentKeyMemory
exports.description:
The key that remounts the current content: it changes whenever the trigger changes (immediately, so the old DOM is never reused
for the new trigger's content), and once more when the payload only arrives on a later render than the trigger did.
Pure over the previous bookkeeping; the renderer keeps the bookkeeping and the counter.

exports.name: ViewportBox
exports.description: A box as `getBoundingClientRect()` gives it.

exports.name: ViewportOffset
exports.description: The offset of the centre of one box from the centre of another, in px; positive is right and down.

exports.name: ViewportSize
exports.description: The two sizes the viewport freezes the popup at while it morphs: where it was, where it is going.

exports.name: createDelayGroup
exports.description: Creates a delay group: the first member opens after the provider's delay, the next ones at once while the group is warm.

exports.name: DelayGroup
exports.description: A tooltip delay group: the shared open delay of the tooltips under one provider, warm while one is open and for `timeoutMs` after.

exports.name: DelayGroupMember
exports.description: What the group tells its members.

exports.name: DelayGroupOptions
exports.description: Options for `createDelayGroup`.

exports.name: DelayScheduler
exports.description: A timer the group can start and cancel; tests pass a fake clock.

exports.name: GroupDelay
exports.description: An open and a close delay, in ms. `undefined` leaves a part to its own default.

exports.name: createHoverIntent
exports.description: Creates the hover-intent state machine for one popup, following the rules at the top of this file.

exports.name: isMouseLike
exports.description: Pointer types that hover: a mouse, or none known yet (a synthetic `mouseenter` before any pointer event).

exports.name: HoverIntent
exports.description: The hover-intent state machine: the DOM layer reports pointer events and it opens or closes the popup on time.

exports.name: HoverIntentOptions
exports.description: What `createHoverIntent` reads: the delays (read at each use) and the popup's state, and how it opens and closes the popup.

exports.name: INSTANT_TYPES
exports.description: The values `data-instant` takes: which kind of change must skip its transition.

exports.name: instantTypeFor
exports.description:
The transition a change skips, as Base UI sets `data-instant`: a keyboard click (Enter or Space on a trigger,
a press with `detail === 0`) is `click`; a popover closed by Escape or by nothing in particular, and a tooltip
closed by a press or Escape, is `dismiss`; focus leaving a popover and focus opening a tooltip are `focus`. A menu
is the popover's rule without the focus case: a keyboard click (on the trigger or an item) is `click`, Escape or
nothing in particular is `dismiss`. Anything else keeps its animation (`undefined`).
exports.signature: (kind: PopupKind, reason: OpenChangeReason | null, open: boolean, keyboardClick: boolean) => InstantType | undefined

exports.name: OPEN_CHANGE_REASONS
exports.description: Every reason an open change carries.

exports.name: openMethodOf
exports.description: The open method of a trigger activation: a pointer's type, else the keyboard when the click carries no pointer (`detail` 0).

exports.name: PATIENT_CLICK_THRESHOLD_MS
exports.description:
A click on a trigger within this long (ms) of the popup opening by hover keeps it open instead of closing it: the click is the user
confirming what the pointer just opened (Base UI's patient click, `PATIENT_CLICK_THRESHOLD`). A later click closes it, as it would a click-opened popup.

exports.name: DialogChangeReason
exports.description: What a dialog, alert dialog or drawer emits: no hover, focus-open, disabled or menu reasons.

exports.name: InstantType
exports.description: One of `INSTANT_TYPES`: the kind of change whose transition is skipped.

exports.name: MenuChangeReason
exports.description: What a menu (and a context menu, and a submenu) emits: the popup reasons without a Close part, plus its own.

exports.name: NavigationMenuChangeReason
exports.description:
What a navigation menu emits (Base UI's `NavigationMenuRoot.ChangeEventReason`): a trigger pressed or hovered, an outside press, an arrow key
on a trigger, focus leaving, Escape, a link pressed (`closeOnClick`), or `none` (a close the host asked for).

exports.name: ComboboxCoreChangeReason
exports.description:
What a combobox and an autocomplete emit (Base UI 1.4.1's `AriaCombobox.ChangeEventReason` and the reasons its input and trigger use): a press or Escape,
an item pressed, an arrow key, focus leaving, the Close part, the text input pressed, typed in or emptied, the clear button and a chip's remove button.
No hover, no focus-open, no sibling menus.

exports.name: OpenChangeReason
exports.description: Why a popup opened or closed: one of `OPEN_CHANGE_REASONS`, passed to `onOpenChange`.

exports.name: OpenMethod
exports.description:
How a layer was opened or closed, for focus decisions: a touch-opened popup focuses the popup itself (no virtual
keyboard). Base UI's `''` ("nobody pressed": a controlled prop, `defaultOpen`) is `OpenMethod | ""` where it applies.

exports.name: PopupChangeReason
exports.description: What a popover, tooltip or preview card emits: no swipe, no close watcher and no menu reasons.

exports.name: PopupKind
exports.description: The popup families that share the open-change machinery.

exports.name: SelectCoreChangeReason
exports.description:
What a select emits besides the one reason only it has, `"window-resize"` (the viewport changed while its popup was laid over the trigger; the type is
`SelectChangeReason` in the react layer, which owns the part): a press or Escape, an item pressed, an arrow key on its trigger, a press-drag let go outside,
focus leaving. No hover, no Close part, no sibling menus.

exports.name: createSafePolygon
exports.description:
One decision maker per hover-out. Feed it every sample from the moment the pointer leaves the trigger; it
remembers whether the pointer has landed on the popup and how fast it is moving.
exports.signature: (context: SafePolygonContext) => (sample: SafePolygonSample, reference: SafeRect, floating: SafeRect) => SafePolygonVerdict

exports.name: CURSOR_SPEED_THRESHOLD
exports.description: Pointer speed under which the pointer counts as stopped, in px per ms.

exports.name: isPointInQuadrilateral
exports.description: Even-odd test of a point against the quadrilateral (x1,y1)-(x2,y2)-(x3,y3)-(x4,y4).
exports.signature: (px: number, py: number, x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number, x3: number, y3: number, x4: number, y4: number) => boolean

exports.name: SAFE_POLYGON_ARM_MS
exports.description: How long a pointer may rest inside the polygon without landing before the popup closes.

exports.name: SafePolygonContext
exports.description: What `createSafePolygon` needs: the side the popup sits on and where the pointer left the trigger.

exports.name: SafePolygonSample
exports.description: One pointer sample: a `mousemove` on the document or the `mouseleave` of the trigger or popup.

exports.name: SafePolygonSide
exports.description: The physical side of the trigger the popup sits on.

exports.name: SafePolygonVerdict
exports.description: What a sample means for the popup.

exports.name: SafeRect
exports.description: A box in viewport pixels.

exports.name: ACCORDION_KEYS
exports.description: Keys an accordion header answers to besides Enter and Space.

exports.name: accordionFocusTarget
exports.description:
The enabled header to focus after `key`, as a position among the enabled headers, or `-1` when the key does
nothing here (Up and Down only move a vertical accordion, Left and Right only a horizontal one, mirrored
under RTL; PageUp and PageDown do nothing). Without `loop` the first and last headers hold. The walk itself
is the roving one (`listMove` / `listIndex`), so an accordion moves exactly as every other roving list.
exports.signature: ({ key, index, count, orientation, rtl, loop }: AccordionFocusInput) => number

exports.name: isAccordionKey
exports.description: True for a key an accordion header handles itself.

exports.name: panelSizeValue
exports.description: A measured panel size as the CSS custom property value styles read: `auto` while unmeasured, else pixels.

exports.name: AccordionFocusInput
exports.description: What `accordionFocusTarget` takes.

exports.name: AccordionKey
exports.description: One of {@link ACCORDION_KEYS}.

exports.name: PanelTransition
exports.description: How a disclosure panel is animating: the first frame of opening, the closing frames, or neither.

exports.name: MIN_THUMB_SIZE
exports.description: The shortest a thumb gets, in px, however long the content.

exports.name: SCROLL_EDGE_TOLERANCE
exports.description: Distance in px within which an offset counts as "at" an edge (sub-pixel scroll positions).

exports.name: SCROLL_TIMEOUT
exports.description: How long after the last scroll movement the area still counts as scrolling, in ms.

exports.name: edgeDistances
exports.description:
Scroll distances from the start and end of each axis, normalised (snapped at the ends). An axis whose
scrollbar is hidden has none, and `offsetX` is the raw `scrollLeft` (negated under RTL).
exports.signature: (viewport: { width: number; height: number; }, content: { width: number; height: number; }, offset: { x: number; y: number; }, hidden: { x: boolean; y: boolean; }, rtl: boolean) => EdgeDistances

exports.name: isAxisHidden
exports.description: True when content fits the viewport, so this axis needs no scrollbar.

exports.name: maxScrollOffset
exports.description: How far past the start edge a scroll may go: content size less viewport size, never negative.

exports.name: maxThumbTravel
exports.description: How far the thumb can travel along its track, px.
exports.signature: (track: number, thumb: number, trackPadding: number, thumbMargin: number) => number

exports.name: normalizeEdgeThreshold
exports.description: A threshold as four non-negative numbers.

exports.name: normalizeScrollOffset
exports.description: `value` clamped to `[0, max]` and snapped to 0 or `max` when within {@link SCROLL_EDGE_TOLERANCE} of it.

exports.name: overflowEdges
exports.description: Which edges have content past them: a distance beyond its threshold, on an axis that overflows.
exports.signature: (distances: EdgeDistances, threshold: Readonly<Record<keyof OverflowEdges, number>>, hidden: { x: boolean; y: boolean; }) => OverflowEdges

exports.name: scrollOffsetFromThumbDrag
exports.description: The scroll position after the thumb was dragged `delta` px from where a drag began at `startOffset`.
exports.signature: (startOffset: number, delta: number, maxTravel: number, content: number, viewport: number) => number

exports.name: scrollOffsetFromTrackPress
exports.description: The scroll position that puts the thumb's centre under a press on the track.
exports.signature: ({ pointer, thumb, trackPadding, thumbMargin, maxTravel, content, viewport, rtl, negativeOffsets }: TrackPressInput) => number

exports.name: thumbLength
exports.description: The thumb's length in px: the viewport/content ratio of the room the track gives it, never under {@link MIN_THUMB_SIZE}.
exports.signature: ({ viewport, content, track, trackPadding, thumbMargin, cornerOffset }: AxisMetrics, hidden: boolean) => number

exports.name: thumbTranslation
exports.description: The thumb's translation in px for a scroll `offset`: proportional to progress through the scroll range, kept inside its track (Safari rubber-bands `scrollTop` past the ends). Negative under RTL horizontal.
exports.signature: (offset: number, scrollRange: number, maxTravel: number, rtl: boolean) => number

exports.name: AxisMetrics
exports.description: One axis of a scroll area, as measured.

exports.name: EdgeDistances
exports.description: Distances (px) from each end of each axis to the content past it.

exports.name: OverflowEdgeThreshold
exports.description: Per-edge thresholds (px of remaining scroll below which an edge counts as reached).

exports.name: OverflowEdges
exports.description: Which ends of each axis still have content past them.

exports.name: TrackPressInput
exports.description: What a press on the track (not the thumb) asks for.

exports.name: clamp
exports.description: `value` limited to `[min, max]`.
exports.signature: (value: number, min: number, max: number) => number

exports.name: formatNumber
exports.description: `value` formatted for `locale` with `Intl.NumberFormat` options. The one number formatter (formatters are cached by locale and options).
exports.signature: (value: number, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions) => string

exports.name: SLIDER_KEYS
exports.description: Keys a thumb answers to.

exports.name: ascending
exports.description: Ascending comparator for `Array.prototype.sort`.

exports.name: decimalPrecision
exports.description: Decimal places needed to write `num` exactly (`0.25` → 2, `1e-8` → 8, `10` → 0).

exports.name: defaultValueText
exports.description:
The `aria-valuetext` a thumb gets when the app gives none: "start range" / "end range" after the value for a
two-thumb range, the formatted value when a `format` is set, otherwise nothing (the native range input
announces its number).
exports.signature: (values: readonly number[], index: number, locale: Intl.LocalesArgument | undefined, format: Intl.NumberFormatOptions | undefined) => string | undefined

exports.name: hasMinimumDistance
exports.description: True when every neighbouring pair of a range is at least `step * minStepsBetweenValues` apart (a single value always is).
exports.signature: (values: number | readonly number[], step: number, minStepsBetweenValues: number) => boolean

exports.name: isSliderKey
exports.description: True for a key a slider thumb handles.

exports.name: nearestThumbIndex
exports.description:
The thumb nearest `pointer` along the slider axis, given each thumb's centre (a later thumb wins a tie, so
pressing past two stacked thumbs picks the one that can still move toward the end). `-1` for no thumbs.

exports.name: pushThumbValues
exports.description: Move thumb `index` to `nextValue` and push its neighbours along so the minimum distance holds.
exports.signature: ({ values, index, nextValue, min, max, step, minStepsBetweenValues, initialValues }: PushedThumbInput) => number[]

exports.name: replaceAt
exports.description: A copy of `array` with `index` replaced, sorted ascending.
exports.signature: (array: readonly number[], index: number, value: number) => number[]

exports.name: resolveThumbCollision
exports.description: Resolve a drag of thumb `pressedIndex` to `nextValue` under a collision behaviour (see {@link ThumbCollisionBehavior}).
exports.signature: ({ behavior, values, currentValues, initialValues, pressedIndex, nextValue, min, max, step, minStepsBetweenValues }: ThumbCollisionInput) => ThumbCollisionResult

exports.name: roundValueToStep
exports.description: The step grid point (`min + n * step`) nearest `value`, without floating point dust (`0.1 * 3` → `0.3`).
exports.signature: (value: number, step: number, min: number) => number

exports.name: sliderKeyValue
exports.description:
The value a key press asks for, or `null` for a key that does nothing: arrows move one `step` (`largeStep`
with Shift; Right and Left swap under RTL), PageUp and PageDown move `largeStep`, Home and End jump to the
ends, a range thumb stopping `step * minStepsBetweenValues` short of its neighbour.
exports.signature: ({ key, shiftKey, values, index, min, max, step, largeStep, minStepsBetweenValues, rtl }: SliderKeyInput) => number | null

exports.name: sliderValueFor
exports.description:
The value a thumb takes when a native `<input type=range>` reports `valueInput`: clamped to `[min, max]`,
and for a range bound to its neighbours then re-sorted into the whole array.
exports.signature: (valueInput: number, index: number, min: number, max: number, range: boolean, values: readonly number[]) => number | number[]

exports.name: sliderValueFromPointer
exports.description: The step-snapped, clamped value under the pointer. Horizontal grows from the left (right under RTL), vertical from the bottom.
exports.signature: ({ x, y, rect, vertical, rtl, offsetStart, offsetEnd, insetThumbOffset, thumbCenterOffset, min, max, step }: SliderPointerInput) => number

exports.name: valuesToPercents
exports.description: {@link valueToPercent} for every value, each clamped to 0–100.
exports.signature: (values: readonly number[], min: number, max: number) => number[]

exports.name: PushedThumbInput
exports.description: What `getPushedThumbValues` takes.

exports.name: SliderKey
exports.description: One of {@link SLIDER_KEYS}.

exports.name: SliderKeyInput
exports.description: What `sliderKeyValue` takes.

exports.name: SliderPointerInput
exports.description: What `sliderValueFromPointer` takes.

exports.name: SliderRect
exports.description: The control's box in the pointer's coordinates.

exports.name: ThumbCollisionBehavior
exports.description: What happens when a dragged thumb meets its neighbour.

exports.name: ThumbCollisionInput
exports.description: What `resolveThumbCollision` takes.

exports.name: ThumbCollisionResult
exports.description: The outcome of moving a thumb: the new value, the thumb that now holds the drag, and whether two thumbs traded places.

exports.name: TAB_ACTIVATION_DIRECTIONS
exports.description: Where the newly selected tab lies relative to the previously selected one.

exports.name: activeTabBox
exports.description:
The active tab's position inside the list for the indicator: its distance from each edge of the list's
scrollable area and its size, undone for any scale an ancestor applies (a scaled dialog) and counting how far
the list has scrolled.
exports.signature: ({ tab, list, tabSize, listSize, listScroll, tabOffset }: ActiveTabBoxInput) => ActiveTabBox

exports.name: isIndicatorVisible
exports.description: Whether the indicator has a size worth showing (not before the layout has settled).

exports.name: shouldActivateOnFocus
exports.description:
Whether focus on a tab selects it. Automatic activation selects on keyboard focus, touch focus and focus from the
main mouse button; a press with another button focuses without selecting.

exports.name: tabActivationDirection
exports.description:
The direction of a selection change: `left` / `right` along a horizontal list, `up` / `down` along a vertical one,
by where the two tabs sit on screen (so a reordered or RTL list reports what the user sees); `none` when nothing
was selected before or after, or the tabs share a position. A tab that is not on screen yet falls back to
comparing the two values when both are numbers or both are strings.
exports.signature: ({ from, to, fromCorner, toCorner, orientation }: TabActivationInput) => TabActivationDirection

exports.name: tabSelectionFallback
exports.description:
The selection to switch to when the selected tab is disabled or has been removed: the first enabled tab in
document order, or `null` when every tab is disabled. Returns `undefined` for "keep the selection": nothing is
registered yet, the value is controlled, a selection of `null` stays `null`, a disabled tab the caller named in
`defaultValue` stays selected, or the replacement is the selection already.
exports.signature: <V>(tabs: readonly TabSummary<V>[], { value, controlled, explicitDefault, defaultValue }: TabFallbackOptions<V>) => { readonly value: V | null; } | undefined

exports.name: ActiveTabBox
exports.description: Where the active tab sits inside the tab list, in the list's own CSS pixels.

exports.name: ActiveTabBoxInput
exports.description: What {@link activeTabBox} takes.

exports.name: DrawnBox
exports.description: A box on screen: its top left corner and its size as drawn (a scaled ancestor makes this differ from the CSS size).

exports.name: FocusActivationInput
exports.description: What {@link shouldActivateOnFocus} takes.

exports.name: TabActivationDirection
exports.description: One of `TAB_ACTIVATION_DIRECTIONS`.

exports.name: TabActivationInput
exports.description: What {@link tabActivationDirection} takes.

exports.name: TabCorner
exports.description: The top left corner of a tab on screen (a DOM rect fits).

exports.name: TabFallbackOptions
exports.description: What {@link tabSelectionFallback} takes besides the tabs.

exports.name: TabSummary
exports.description: A registered tab, as selection sees it.

exports.name: TabsOrientation
exports.description: Which way the tab list runs.

exports.name: CONTEXT_MENU_LONG_PRESS_MS
exports.description: A touch held this long on a context-menu trigger opens the menu; a right-button release before it never activates an item.

exports.name: CONTEXT_MENU_RELEASE_SLOP
exports.description: A release within this distance (px) of the point the context menu opened at is the opening gesture's own release.

exports.name: CONTEXT_MENU_TOUCH_SLOP
exports.description: A touch that moves farther than this (px, either axis) is a scroll, not a long press.

exports.name: MENU_ITEM_KINDS
exports.description: What an item does when activated: run an action, toggle a checkbox, pick a radio.

exports.name: MENU_MOUSEUP_DELAY_MS
exports.description: A mouse press on the trigger released over an item this soon after opening does not activate it (a click, not a drag).

exports.name: MENU_SUBMENU_DELAY_MS
exports.description: How long the pointer rests on a submenu trigger before the submenu opens (Base UI's `delay`).

exports.name: MENU_TRIGGER_HOVER_DELAY_MS
exports.description: How long the pointer rests on a menu's own trigger (`openOnHover`) before the menu opens (Base UI's `delay`, 100 ms).

exports.name: closesOnActivate
exports.description:
Whether activating an item closes its menu (and every menu above it). An action closes; a checkbox or a radio
stays open so several can be set in one visit. `closeOnClick` overrides the default for any kind.

exports.name: menuFocusOnOpen
exports.description:
Where focus lands on open. From the keyboard the first item is highlighted (ArrowUp on the trigger: the last); a
pointer focuses the popup and highlights nothing, so the next arrow key starts at an end; a submenu opened by hover
leaves focus on its trigger, so the pointer can keep moving through the parent menu; a menu a menubar opened because
focus walked onto its trigger highlights its first item.

exports.name: menuItemRole
exports.description: The ARIA role for an item kind: `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`.

exports.name: menuKeyCommand
exports.description:
The command for `event` in a menu, or null when the menu leaves the key alone (Tab, Escape and typed characters
are the layer's and the typeahead's). The inline keys follow the text direction: in RTL ← opens a submenu.
PageUp / PageDown do not move in a menu (Base UI's list navigation has no page jump).

exports.name: menuMoveIndex
exports.description:
The index a move lands on from `current` (-1: nothing highlighted, the popup has focus), or null when it stays. From
nothing, `next` starts at the first item and `prev` at the last, as an arrow key in a pointer-opened menu does.
exports.signature: (move: NavMove, current: number, options: MenuMoveOptions) => number | null

exports.name: menuTriggerKey
exports.description: The arrow key on a menu trigger that opens the menu, and which end it lands on (APG Menu Button).

exports.name: MenuFocusOnOpen
exports.description: Where focus goes when a menu opens: an item at either end, the popup itself, or nowhere (it stays put).

exports.name: MenuItemKind
exports.description: One of `MENU_ITEM_KINDS`: an action item, a checkbox item or a radio item.

exports.name: MenuItemRole
exports.description: The ARIA role of each item kind.

exports.name: MenuKeyCommand
exports.description: What a key does inside an open menu. `move` goes through the roving maths; the rest are menu rules.

exports.name: MenuKeyContext
exports.description: What `menuKeyCommand` needs besides the key: the orientation, the text direction and where the menu sits.

exports.name: MenuMoveOptions
exports.description: Options for `menuMoveIndex`: the item count, wrapping and which items are disabled.

exports.name: MenuOpenFacts
exports.description: What `menuFocusOnOpen` needs to decide where focus goes when a menu opens.

exports.name: menubarHasSubmenuOpen
exports.description:
Whether any menu of the bar is open after a menu opened or closed. A menu opening makes it true. One closing makes it false,
unless it closed because the bar is moving to another menu (`sibling-open`: another menu opened; `list-navigation`: an arrow key
walked off it), in which case the bar still has a menu open or is about to.
exports.signature: (current: boolean, change: { readonly open: boolean; readonly reason: OpenChangeReason | null; }) => boolean

exports.name: menubarHoverOpens
exports.description:
Whether the pointer resting on a trigger opens its menu. Only while another menu of the bar is open (Base UI's rule: the bar walks between its menus as the pointer
does, and never opens one from rest); `openOnHover={false}` takes a trigger out of the walk.

exports.name: menubarTriggerKey
exports.description:
The key on a menubar trigger that opens its menu, and which end of the menu focus lands on. In a horizontal bar the arrow
that points into the menu opens it on the first item (ArrowDown), and ArrowUp opens it on the last (APG: optional); in a
vertical bar the inline-end arrow does (the menu opens beside the bar), mirrored in RTL.
exports.signature: (event: NavKey, orientation: MenubarOrientation, dir?: TextDirection) => "first" | "last" | null

exports.name: MenubarOrientation
exports.description: The two orientations of a menubar.

exports.name: textFieldKeepsKey
exports.description:
Whether a text field keeps `event` for itself. A field moves its own caret with the arrow keys, so the toolbar takes a key only
when the caret has nowhere left to go in that direction: Shift (extending a selection) and a selection that is not collapsed belong
to the field, the key that moves forward stays with the field until the caret is at the end of the text, the key that moves back until it is at the
start, and Home and End are always the field's (they move the caret to the ends of the line). A field with no selection
(`selectionStart` null) is not a text field for this rule: the toolbar takes the key.
exports.signature: (event: NavKey, caret: TextFieldCaret, options: { readonly orientation: RovingOrientation; readonly dir?: TextDirection; }) => boolean

exports.name: toolbarItemDisabled
exports.description:
Whether an item is disabled: the toolbar, its group or the item itself says so. A disabled toolbar disables every
button and input in it, a disabled group the ones inside it.
exports.signature: (facts: { readonly toolbar: boolean; readonly group?: boolean; readonly own: boolean; }) => boolean

exports.name: toolbarItemSkipped
exports.description:
Whether the arrow keys step over an item. A disabled item stays a stop of the toolbar (it can be focused and its name read)
unless it opted out with `focusableWhenDisabled={false}`; a link can never be disabled.
exports.signature: (facts: { readonly disabled: boolean; readonly focusableWhenDisabled: boolean; }) => boolean

exports.name: toolbarSeparatorOrientation
exports.description: The orientation of a toolbar's separator: perpendicular to the toolbar, so a horizontal toolbar has vertical dividers.

exports.name: TextFieldCaret
exports.description: The caret of a text field: where its selection starts and ends (null: the field has no selection, such as `type=number`) and how long its text is.

exports.name: blockingFields
exports.description:
The fields that block a submit, in registration order: every one not known to be valid. That includes a field whose
(asynchronous) validation is still pending (`null`): the submit waits for it, as in Base UI, and the user submits again
once it has settled.

exports.name: clearFormError
exports.description: A form's external errors without `name`, or the same object when it held none for it.

exports.name: collectFormValues
exports.description: The named fields' values, by name.

exports.name: combineValidity
exports.description: The validity data with the external `invalid` flag folded into `state.valid`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_FIELD_STATE
exports.description: The state of a field with nothing known about it: what a control outside any `Field` reads.

exports.name: DEFAULT_VALIDITY_STATE
exports.description: A field that has not been validated: every flag off and `valid` unknown.

exports.name: describedByIds
exports.description: The ids a control is described by: the enclosing fields' messages first, then its own. `undefined` when there are none.
exports.signature: (parentIds: readonly string[], ownIds: readonly string[]) => string | undefined

exports.name: fieldStateAttributes
exports.description: Every state attribute a field's state writes, for a part that has no renderer of its own (the form kit's field shell, a native target).

exports.name: fieldValidityAttributes
exports.description: `data-valid` or `data-invalid` for a known validity, nothing while it is `null`. (The other flags are plain booleans: `data-touched`, `data-dirty`, `data-filled`, `data-focused`, `data-disabled`.)

exports.name: hasFormError
exports.description: Whether `errors` (a form's external errors) holds an entry for `name`.

exports.name: invalidFields
exports.description: The fields known to be invalid, in registration order (a pending one, `null`, is not): where focus goes when new errors arrive.

exports.name: isOnlyValueMissing
exports.description: True when `valueMissing` is the only constraint that fails (an empty required field).

exports.name: nativeValidityState
exports.description:
The validity a field reports for a native snapshot. A lone `valueMissing` (an empty required field) only counts
once the field was marked dirty (the user changed it, or a submit validated it), so a form does not shout at
fields nobody has touched.

exports.name: resolveFieldValid
exports.description: A field is valid unless something external marks it invalid; `null` stays `null` (not validated yet).

exports.name: resultMessages
exports.description: The messages a `validate` result stands for.

exports.name: shouldValidateOnChange
exports.description:
Whether a change validates: always in `onChange` mode; in `onSubmit` mode once a submit was attempted (a field the
user is fixing after a failed submit clears its error as they type).

exports.name: snapshotValidity
exports.description: A copy of a constraint's validity flags.

exports.name: validateField
exports.description:
Validate one field: the browser's constraints first, then (when they pass, or on change) the caller's `validate`
function. It sets the control's custom validity to the message(s) so the browser agrees with the state. Returns the
outcome, or `null` when the pass changes nothing (a revalidation that has nothing to say). The result is
synchronous unless `validate` returned a promise: a form reads it synchronously on submit, so a field whose
`validate` is synchronous must settle in the same call.

exports.name: VALIDITY_KEYS
exports.description: The keys of a `ValidityState` (plus `valid`), in the order Base UI lists them.

exports.name: FieldStateFlags
exports.description: What a field exposes as state: the Base UI field state, `valid` being `null` until known.

exports.name: FieldValidate
exports.description: A field's custom validation; it may be asynchronous (an async result never blocks a submit).

exports.name: FieldValidateResult
exports.description: The `validate` function result: a message, several, or `null` for valid.

exports.name: FieldValidationMode
exports.description: When a field validates: on submit (and, once a submit was attempted, on every change), on blur, or on every change.

exports.name: FieldValidityData
exports.description: What validating a field produced.

exports.name: FieldValidityState
exports.description: A field's validity: the browser's `ValidityState` flags, and `valid` as `null` until the field has been validated.

props.name: badInput
props.description: Whether the browser cannot convert the input (a half-typed number or date).

props.name: customError
props.description: Whether a custom message was set (`setCustomValidity` or the `validate` function).

props.name: patternMismatch
props.description: Whether the value does not match `pattern`.

props.name: rangeOverflow
props.description: Whether the value is above `max`.

props.name: rangeUnderflow
props.description: Whether the value is below `min`.

props.name: stepMismatch
props.description: Whether the value does not fit `step`.

props.name: tooLong
props.description: Whether the value is longer than `maxLength`.

props.name: tooShort
props.description: Whether the value is shorter than `minLength`.

props.name: typeMismatch
props.description: Whether the value does not fit the input's `type` (an email or a URL).

props.name: valueMissing
props.description: Whether a `required` field is empty.

props.name: valid
props.description: Whether the field is valid; `null` until it has been validated.

exports.name: FormErrors
exports.description: Errors a form is given from outside (a server), keyed by field name.

exports.name: FormFieldEntry
exports.description: One field as a form knows it.

exports.name: NativeConstraint
exports.description: Something that carries native constraint validity: an `<input>` does; so does a stand-in.

exports.name: ValidationOutcome
exports.description: What one validation pass produced.

exports.name: ValidationRequest
exports.description: What one validation pass is given.

exports.name: ValidityKey
exports.description: One key of `VALIDITY_KEYS`: a `ValidityState` flag or `valid`.

exports.name: parentCheckboxState
exports.description: The parent's state: checked when every child is ticked, indeterminate when some but not all are.
exports.signature: (allValues: readonly string[], value: readonly string[]) => ParentCheckboxState

exports.name: parentCheckboxStateOfCount
exports.description: The parent's state from counts: checked when every child is ticked, indeterminate when some but not all are.

exports.name: parentTriState
exports.description: All, some or none of `total` ticked: the one reading of "a parent over many boxes" the form kit's permission matrix and auth's role matrix share.

exports.name: parentChildId
exports.description: The id of the root element (the `role="checkbox"`) of the child checkbox `childValue` under the parent `parentId`; the parent's `aria-controls` lists them. A child's hidden input has its own id, which a label's `for` points at.

exports.name: parentControls
exports.description: The parent's `aria-controls`: the ids of every child.

exports.name: sameItems
exports.description: Two arrays hold the same items in the same order.
exports.signature: (a: readonly unknown[], b: readonly unknown[]) => boolean

exports.name: toggleChild
exports.description: The group's value after the child `childValue` is ticked or cleared, and the cycle to keep (a hand arrangement resets the parent's cycle).
exports.signature: (value: readonly string[], childValue: string, checked: boolean) => { value: string[]; cycle: ParentCycle; }

exports.name: toggleParent
exports.description: The group's next value after the parent is activated, and the cycle to keep.
exports.signature: ({ allValues, value, cycle, isDisabled }: ParentToggleInput) => { value: string[]; cycle: ParentCycle; }

exports.name: ParentCheckboxState
exports.description: What the parent checkbox looks like for a value.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the parent shows as checked: every child is ticked.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Whether the parent shows as mixed: some children are ticked but not all.

exports.name: ParentCycle
exports.description: What the parent keeps between presses.

exports.name: ParentCycleStatus
exports.description: Where the parent's three-press cycle stands: `mixed` (hand-picked), then `on` (all), then `off` (none).

exports.name: ParentToggleInput
exports.description: What `toggleParent` needs to work out the group's next value when the parent is activated.

exports.name: ParentTriState
exports.description: The same three states under the names a grant matrix uses: `all`, `some` (the mixed one) or `none` (also when there is nothing to tick).

exports.name: clampNumber
exports.description: `value` held inside `[min, max]` (either bound may be missing).
exports.signature: (value: number, min?: number, max?: number) => number

exports.name: commitNumber
exports.description: A typed value through a formatter's parse, then held inside `[min, max]`; null stays null.
exports.signature: (text: string, formatter: NumberFormatter, locale: Intl.LocalesArgument | undefined, options: NumberFormatOptions | undefined, min?: number, max?: number) => number | null

exports.name: decimalsOf
exports.description: Digits after the decimal point of a number, exponent notation included (1e-7 → 7).

exports.name: formatPrecision
exports.description: The decimals the formatter shows for a value (percent adds two, since the value is a fraction).

exports.name: intlNumberFormatter
exports.description:
The default number formatter: Intl formatting, locale-aware parsing
({@link parseNumber}), rounded to the decimals the format shows, so the
committed value is exactly the one on screen.

exports.name: isPartialNumber
exports.description: True while `text` could still become a number in `locale` (empty, "-", "12,"), so a field can refuse other keystrokes.
exports.signature: (text: string, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: NumberFormatOptions) => boolean

exports.name: MINUS_SIGNS
exports.description: Characters people type for "minus": hyphen-minus, the Unicode minus sign, figure and en dashes, small and full-width hyphen-minus.

exports.name: numberFieldKeyAction
exports.description:
The spinbutton key table (WAI-ARIA spinbutton): ↑/↓ step, Shift+↑/↓ and
PageUp/PageDown take the large step, Home/End go to min/max. Returns null for
every other key, so typing stays the input's own.

exports.name: numberFormat
exports.description: A cached `Intl.NumberFormat` for one locale + options pair (a field formats on every keystroke).

exports.name: numberSymbols
exports.description: The group and decimal separators, affixes and digits for a locale + options pair (cached).

exports.name: parseNumber
exports.description:
Reads typed text in `locale` back into a number, or null when it is empty, a
lone sign or not a number. Group separators are dropped wherever they are, the
locale's decimal separator is the only one read as decimal, any minus variant
works, and currency, unit and percent affixes are ignored. With
`style: "percent"` the result is the shown number ÷ 100 ("15 %" → 0.15). No
rounding and no clamping; see {@link intlNumberFormatter} for those.
exports.signature: (text: string, locale?: Intl.LocalesArgument, options?: NumberFormatOptions) => number | null

exports.name: removeFloatingPointErrors
exports.description:
`value` rounded to the decimals the format keeps (its maximum, at least its minimum), so float noise (0.30000000000000004)
never reaches a value; without a format's maximum it keeps 15 significant digits, the most a double holds exactly.

exports.name: roundTo
exports.description: `n` rounded to `digits` decimals, with the binary noise removed (0.1 + 0.2 → 0.3).

exports.name: snapToStep
exports.description:
The grid point at or beyond `value`: `mode` "directional" moves toward the sign of `step` (floor for a step up,
ceil for a step down), "nearest" rounds. The grid starts at `base`.
exports.signature: (value: number, base: number, step: number, mode?: "directional" | "nearest") => number

exports.name: toValidatedNumber
exports.description:
Base UI's value validation: clamp to `[min, max]`, snap to the step's multiples when a step was taken and
`snapOnStep` is on (from `min`, or from 0 without one or for the small step), then drop float noise. Null stays null.
exports.signature: (value: number | null, { step, snapGrid, format, min, max, snapOnStep, small, clamp: shouldClamp }?: ValidateNumberOptions) => number | null

exports.name: NumberFieldKeyAction
exports.description: What a key does on a number spinbutton.

exports.name: NumberFormatOptions
exports.description: The Intl options a number field formats with (decimal, currency, percent, unit…).

exports.name: NumberFormatter
exports.description:
How a number field turns its value into text and typed text back into a
value. Default: {@link intlNumberFormatter} (Intl, any locale). Swap it for a
domain format (a "1.2k" shorthand, a duration "1h 30m", a fixed-point money
type) without touching the field.

exports.name: NumberSymbols
exports.description: The symbols one locale + options combination writes.

exports.name: ValidateNumberOptions
exports.description: What {@link toValidatedNumber} needs.

exports.name: DEFAULT_METER_MAX
exports.description: The default `max` (see {@link MeterRange.max}).

exports.name: formatMeterValue
exports.description:
The value as text for Base UI's `Meter.Root`: `value` itself through `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, format)`; without
`format` a percentage of 100 (so 50 reads "50%"), like Progress's.
exports.signature: (value: number, locale: Intl.LocalesArgument | undefined, format: Intl.NumberFormatOptions | undefined) => string

exports.name: meterState
exports.description: The resolved range with its percentage (clamped: the value is) and zone.

exports.name: meterValueText
exports.description: The default `aria-valuetext` of `Meter.Root`: the formatted value when a `format` is given, else `value%`.
exports.signature: (formattedValue: string, value: number, hasFormat: boolean) => string

exports.name: meterZone
METER_ZONES
exports.description: The three regions of a meter's range, best first (HTML calls the last one "even less good").

exports.name: percentMeterFormat
exports.description: The default: the rounded percent of the range ("62%").

exports.name: resolveMeter
exports.description:
Resolves the boundaries the way the HTML spec does: `max` below `min` becomes
`min`; `value` and `optimum` clamp into [min, max]; `low` clamps into
[min, max]; `high` clamps into [low, max]. A NaN or missing value reads as min.

exports.name: MeterFormatter
exports.description:
Turns a meter's state into the text a screen reader hears (aria-valuetext)
and the Value part shows: "7.2 GB of 10 GB", "Strong", "62%". The seam for
units and locales.

exports.name: MeterRange
exports.description: A meter's inputs; everything but `value` is optional, with the `<meter>` element's defaults.

exports.name: MeterState
exports.description: Everything a meter's parts read, computed once per render.

props.name: percent
props.description: Where the value sits in the range, 0 to 100 (0 when `min` equals `max`).

props.name: zone
props.description: The region the value is in.

props.name: value
props.description: The value, clamped to `min`..`max`.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range, never below `min`.

props.name: low
props.description: The upper end of the low region, clamped to the range.

props.name: high
props.description: The lower end of the high region, clamped to `low`..`max`.

props.name: optimum
props.description: The best value, clamped to the range.

exports.name: MeterZone
exports.description: One of `METER_ZONES`: `optimum`, `suboptimal` or `critical`.

exports.name: ResolvedMeter
exports.description: A range with every boundary resolved and clamped, as the HTML algorithm does before it compares.

exports.name: backspaceOtp
exports.description: Backspace at slot `index`: clears that slot when filled, else the one before it.

exports.name: insertOtp
exports.description:
Text arriving at slot `index` (one typed key, an autofill, or a paste): it
fills from that slot onward, overwriting, and focus moves past the last
character written. A value never has holes, so writing past the end appends.
exports.signature: (value: string, index: number, text: string, length: number, charset?: OtpCharset) => OtpEdit

exports.name: normalizeOtpValue
exports.description:
User-entered code text as a value: whitespace gone, the validation type's strip (or the host's `sanitizeValue` for
`none`) applied, then cut to `length` characters (by code point, so a multi-byte character never splits across slots).
exports.signature: (value: string | null | undefined, length: number, type?: OTPValidationType, sanitizeValue?: (value: string) => string) => string

exports.name: OTP_PATTERNS
exports.description: The characters each charset accepts, one character per match.

exports.name: otpActiveIndex
exports.description: The slot a caret rests on: the one the next character goes into (the last once the code is full).

exports.name: otpComplete
exports.description: Whether every slot is filled.

exports.name: otpValidationConfig
exports.description: The rules of a validation type, or `null` for `none` (the host's `sanitizeValue` decides).

exports.name: removeOtpCharacter
exports.description: The value without the character in slot `index` (unchanged when there is none there).

exports.name: replaceOtpValue
exports.description: Characters written from slot `index` onward over the current value, kept contiguous and at most `length` long.
exports.signature: (current: string, index: number, text: string, length: number, type?: OTPValidationType, sanitizeValue?: (value: string) => string) => string

exports.name: sanitizeOtp
exports.description: Keeps only accepted characters (upper-cased for alphanumeric), at most `length`.
exports.signature: (input: string, length: number, charset?: OtpCharset) => string

exports.name: stripOtpWhitespace
exports.description: The text without any whitespace (people paste codes written "123 456").

exports.name: OTPValidationConfig
exports.description: The slot rules of one validation type: the pattern a slot and the whole code must match, the soft-keyboard hint and what to strip.

exports.name: OTPValidationType
exports.description: What a slot accepts: digits, letters, letters and digits, or anything a `sanitizeValue` lets through (`none`).

exports.name: OtpCharset
exports.description: Which characters a slot accepts in the pickers API.

exports.name: OtpEdit
exports.description: The result of an edit (`insertOtp`, `backspaceOtp`): the new value and the slot to focus.

exports.name: clampPage
exports.description:
`page` limited to `1..totalPages` (at least 1 when the total is unknown or 0). A non-finite or fractional page is
floored, NaN reads as 1: a controlled pager fed a stale page after the list shrank lands on the last page instead
of an empty one.

exports.name: pageCount
exports.description: How many pages `totalItems` fill at `pageSize` per page (0 items is 0 pages; a size below 1 counts as 1).

exports.name: paginationRange
exports.description:
The items a pager draws, in order. Examples with the defaults (one sibling, one boundary page):
  page 1 of 50  → 1 2 3 4 5 … 50
  page 25 of 50 → 1 … 24 25 26 … 50
  page 50 of 50 → 1 … 46 47 48 49 50
  page 4 of 7   → 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 (fits, no ellipsis)
  page 3 of ∞   → 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 …
exports.signature: ({ page, totalPages, siblingCount, boundaryCount }: PaginationRangeOptions) => PaginationRangeItem[]

exports.name: paginationWidth
exports.description: The number of items {@link paginationRange} returns once the total is larger than it (the pager's fixed width).

exports.name: PaginationRangeItem
exports.description: One entry of a pager: a page number (1-based) or an ellipsis standing for the hidden pages on that side.

exports.name: PaginationRangeOptions
exports.description: What {@link paginationRange} takes.

exports.name: clampRating
exports.description:
`value` kept inside `[0, max]` and snapped to the step (a 3.7 from outside becomes 3.5 with halves, 4 without),
so a controlled value that is not a step never draws an item partly or checks two radios. A non-finite value is 0.

exports.name: ratingCheckedIndex
exports.description:
The 1-based item that is the checked radio for `value`: the item the value ends in (`ceil`, so 2.5 checks item 3),
or 0 when nothing is rated. Exactly one item is checked at a time, as the radio group pattern requires.

exports.name: ratingFromPointer
exports.description:
The value a pointer over item `index` means. `fraction` is how far along the item the pointer is from its
physical left edge (0 to 1); in right-to-left text the item's start is its right edge, so the fraction is mirrored.
Without `allowHalf` the whole item is the item's value; with it, the start half is `index - 0.5`.
exports.signature: (index: number, fraction: number, options: RatingOptions, direction: Direction) => number

exports.name: ratingItemFill
exports.description: How full item `index` (1-based) is drawn while `value` is shown (the chosen value, or the one the pointer previews).

exports.name: ratingItems
exports.description: The values the items stand for, 1 to `max` (an empty list for a `max` under 1).

exports.name: ratingKeyValue
exports.description:
The value after `key`, or `null` when the key means nothing to a rating (the caller then leaves the event alone).
- ArrowRight / ArrowUp raise by one step, ArrowLeft / ArrowDown lower it; in right-to-left text the left and right
  arrows swap (the scale runs from the right), up and down never do.
- Home goes to the lowest rating (one step), End to `max`.
The value stops at the ends instead of wrapping as an APG radio group does: a rating is an ordered scale, and
wrapping from 5 stars to half a star on one more ArrowRight would throw the rating away (Ark's RatingGroup and
MUI's Rating stop too). Lowering never goes below one step from the keyboard: 0 means "not rated", which the
keyboard cannot choose on a radio group (no radio stands for it); `clearable` on the react part handles clearing.
exports.signature: (key: string, value: number, options: RatingOptions, direction: Direction) => number | null

exports.name: ratingStep
exports.description: The smallest change of value: 0.5 with `allowHalf`, else 1.

exports.name: RatingFill
exports.description: How full one item is drawn for a given value: `full` up to the value, `half` for the item a half value ends in.

exports.name: RatingKey
exports.description: The keys a rating answers (`KeyboardEvent.key` values).

exports.name: RatingOptions
exports.description: The bounds and step every rating function reads.

exports.name: applyMask
exports.description:
Lays `raw` into the mask. Only token characters count: a character a slot refuses is dropped (so a raw value
with stray spaces still formats), and characters past the last slot are cut.
exports.signature: (raw: string, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => MaskResult

exports.name: caretAfterEdit
exports.description:
Where the caret goes after an edit: after the same number of token characters it was after in the edited
text. `edited` is the input's text right after the browser applied the edit, `caret` its caret there, and
`next` the reformatted display.
exports.signature: (edited: string, next: string, caret: number, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => number

exports.name: caretAfterTokens
exports.description:
The index in `display` just after its `count`-th token character, or 0 when `count` is 0. With the placeholder
pattern shown, the caret moves on past the literals that follow (the leading ones too), to the next empty slot.
exports.signature: (display: string, count: number, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => number

exports.name: isMaskComplete
exports.description: Every required slot of the mask is filled by `raw`.
exports.signature: (raw: string, mask: Mask, options?: MaskOptions) => boolean

exports.name: MASK_TOKENS
exports.description: The built-in tokens (Mantine's alphabet): `9` digit, `a` letter, `A` letter upper-cased, `*` letter or digit, `#` digit or sign.

exports.name: maskDeleteBackward
exports.description:
Backspace with the masks' rule: with a selection, the token characters in it are removed; with a caret, the
token character before it is removed, even when a literal sits right before the caret (so Backspace over a
space or a bracket deletes the digit before it, instead of only moving the caret).
