exports.signature: (state: MaskEditState, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => MaskEdit

exports.name: maskDeleteForward
exports.description: Delete with the masks' rule: as {@link maskDeleteBackward}, removing the token character after the caret.
exports.signature: (state: MaskEditState, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => MaskEdit

exports.name: maskInputChange
exports.description:
Re-formats the text the browser left in the input after any edit (typing, a paste, a cut, autofill, undo,
a drop) and keeps the caret after the same token character. Typing into a value that already fills every
slot is refused (the previous value comes back with the caret where it was), so a full card number does not
shift its digits off the end; any other edit that brings too many characters is cut at the last slot.
exports.signature: (edited: string, caret: number, previous: MaskEditState, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => MaskEdit

exports.name: maskInsert
exports.description:
Inserts text (typed or pasted) at the selection. The text is aligned with the mask from the slot the caret is
at, so a formatted paste lines up its literals and a raw one fills slot by slot; a full field refuses more.
exports.signature: (state: MaskEditState, text: string, mask: Mask, options?: ApplyMaskOptions) => MaskEdit

exports.name: parseMask
exports.description:
Reads a static mask into slots. In a string, each token character becomes a slot, `\` makes the next character
a literal and `?` marks every slot after it optional. In an array, a `RegExp` is a slot and every character of
a string is a literal.

exports.name: parseMaskFor
exports.description: The parsed mask for a raw value (see {@link resolveMask}).
exports.signature: (mask: Mask, raw: string, tokens?: MaskTokens) => ParsedMask

exports.name: resolveMask
exports.description: The static mask for a raw value: a function mask is called with it, a static one is returned as is.

exports.name: tokensBefore
exports.description: How many token characters sit before `caret` in `display` (the caret's place in the raw value).
exports.signature: (display: string, caret: number, mask: Mask, options?: MaskOptions & { placeholderChar?: string; }) => number

exports.name: unmask
exports.description: Reads the raw value back out of a display string (or any text: formatted, raw or mixed).
exports.signature: (display: string, mask: Mask, options?: MaskOptions & { placeholderChar?: string; }) => string

exports.name: ApplyMaskOptions
exports.description: Options of {@link applyMask}.

exports.name: Mask
exports.description: Any mask: static, or chosen from the raw value.

exports.name: MaskEdit
exports.description: One edit of a masked value and where the caret lands.

exports.name: MaskEditState
exports.description: The state of the input before an edit: its display, the raw value and the selection.

props.name: display
props.description: The text the input shows, mask literals included.

props.name: selectionStart
props.description: Where the selection starts in `display`.

props.name: selectionEnd
props.description: Where the selection ends in `display` (equal to `selectionStart` for a caret).

exports.name: MaskOptions
exports.description: Options shared by the formatting functions.

exports.name: MaskPattern
exports.description: A static mask: a string in the token alphabet, or an array of literals and `RegExp` slots.

exports.name: MaskResult
exports.description: What {@link applyMask} returns.

exports.name: MaskSlot
exports.description: A parsed slot: a token the person fills, or a literal the mask writes.

props.name: kind
props.description:
A token slot: the person types a character the token accepts.
A literal slot: the mask writes `char` itself.

props.name: optional
props.description:
Whether the slot is in the optional tail (after `?`): the value is complete without it.
Whether the slot is in the optional tail (after `?`).

exports.name: MaskToken
exports.description: One token of the mask alphabet: what a slot accepts and how an accepted character is rewritten.

exports.name: MaskTokenInput
exports.description: A custom token: a pattern alone, or a pattern with its transform.

exports.name: MaskTokens
exports.description: The token alphabet by its character in a string mask.

exports.name: ParsedMask
exports.description: A parsed mask: its slots in order.

exports.name: INLINE_EDIT_START_KEYS
exports.description: Keys on the shown value that start editing: Enter, and F2 as in spreadsheets.

exports.name: initialInlineEditState
exports.description: The idle state: nothing being edited.

exports.name: inlineEditKeyAction
exports.description:
The editor's key table: Escape cancels; Enter submits a single-line editor,
while a multi-line one keeps Enter for new lines and submits on Ctrl/⌘+Enter.
Shift+Enter in a single-line editor still submits (there is no new line to type).
exports.signature: (key: string, { multiline, mod }?: { readonly multiline?: boolean; readonly mod?: boolean; }) => InlineEditKeyAction | null

exports.name: inlineEditReducer
exports.description: The state after `event` (see file header). Events that make no sense in the current state return it unchanged.

exports.name: planSubmit
exports.description:
Plans a submit of `draft` against `before`: `busy` while one is pending,
`invalid` when `validate` returns a message, `unchanged` when the draft equals
the value from before editing (by `equals`, default `Object.is`), else `submit`.
exports.signature: <T>(state: InlineEditState<T>, draft: T, before: T, validate?: (draft: T) => string | null | undefined, equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean) => InlineEditSubmitPlan<T>

exports.name: submitErrorMessage
exports.description: The message shown for a rejected `onSubmit`: an Error's message, a string as is, else a generic line.

exports.name: InlineEditEvent
exports.description: What the inline-edit reducer reacts to: an edit starting, a draft change, a refusal, and the steps of a submit.

exports.name: InlineEditKeyAction
exports.description: What a key does in the editor.

exports.name: InlineEditSession
exports.description: One open edit: the value when editing began and the draft being typed.

props.name: session
props.description: The open edit, or null while the value is only shown.

props.name: error
props.description: The message from `validate` or a failed `onSubmit`; cleared by the next change.

props.name: pending
props.description: An async `onSubmit` is running; the editor is read-only meanwhile.

exports.name: InlineEditSubmitPlan
exports.description: What a submit should do, decided before any side effect.

exports.name: isGroupMoveKey
exports.description: True when `event` is a key this group navigates with, whether or not there is anywhere to go.

exports.name: groupMoveTarget
exports.description:
The index focus moves to when `event` is pressed on item `current`, or `null` when the key is not a
navigation key for this group, the group has no other enabled item, or the edge is reached without `loop`.
`current` may be -1 (focus is in the group but on no item): the next key then lands on the first enabled
item and the previous key on the last.
exports.signature: (event: NavKey, current: number, options: GroupMoveOptions) => number | null

exports.name: groupTabStop
exports.description:
The one item that is a tab stop (`tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`): the first of `preferred` that is a valid
enabled index (the item that holds focus, the checked radio, the item last focused), else the first enabled
item, else `null` (every item disabled: nothing to tab to).
exports.signature: (count: number, isDisabled: (index: number) => boolean, preferred?: ReadonlyArray<number | null | undefined>) => number | null

exports.name: GroupMoveOptions
exports.description: What a group needs to know to move focus.

exports.name: listMove
exports.description: The move a key means in a 1D list (K63), or `null` when it is not a navigation key.

exports.name: gridMove
exports.description: The move a key means in a 2D grid (K64): arrows by cell, Home / End by row, Ctrl+Home / End to the corners.

exports.name: listIndex
exports.description:
Where `move` lands from `current` in a 1D list (K63, K66). `current` is -1
when nothing is active yet: `next` then lands on the first item, `prev` on
the last. Returns `null` for no move; never an index outside `0 … count - 1`.
exports.signature: (move: NavMove, current: number, options: ListIndexOptions) => number | null

exports.name: gridIndex
exports.description:
Where `move` lands from `current` in a 2D grid (K64, K66). Up / Down keep the
column, stepping over disabled cells in that column; Down into a short last
row lands on its last item (the cell below does not exist). `null` = no move.
exports.signature: (move: NavMove, current: number, options: GridIndexOptions) => number | null

exports.name: isTypeaheadKey
exports.description:
A single printable character with no Ctrl, Meta or Alt: a typeahead key. A
space only continues a search already in progress (alone it activates).

exports.name: createTypeahead
exports.description:
Typeahead per WAI-ARIA: characters typed within `timeout` of each other build
a prefix searched from the current item; the same character repeated cycles
through the items starting with it. Matching is case-insensitive and wraps.

exports.name: ROVING_ORIENTATIONS
exports.description: Which arrows move in a 1D list: one axis, or all four (a wrapping toolbar or a radio group).

exports.name: RovingOrientation
exports.description: One of `ROVING_ORIENTATIONS`.

exports.name: TEXT_DIRECTIONS
exports.description: Text direction; `rtl` mirrors Left and Right so "next" is always reading order (K67).

exports.name: TextDirection
exports.description: One of `TEXT_DIRECTIONS`.

exports.name: DISABLED_POLICIES
exports.description:
What a disabled item does (K66): `skip` (menus, toolbars: navigation steps
over it) or `focusable` (listboxes and grids per WAI-ARIA: it takes focus so
a screen reader can announce it, but cannot be activated).

exports.name: DisabledPolicy
exports.description: One of `DISABLED_POLICIES`.

exports.name: NAV_MOVES
exports.description: Every move a key can mean; 1D uses the first six, a grid all but `next` / `prev`.

exports.name: NavMove
exports.description: One of `NAV_MOVES`.

exports.name: NavKey
exports.description: The parts of a key event navigation reads; a DOM `KeyboardEvent` fits.

exports.name: DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
exports.description: How many items PageUp / PageDown jump in a list when the host gives no page size.

exports.name: DEFAULT_PAGE_ROWS
exports.description: How many rows PageUp / PageDown jump in a grid when the host gives none.

exports.name: DEFAULT_TYPEAHEAD_TIMEOUT_MS
exports.description: Typeahead buffer lifetime: WAI-ARIA's listbox example and React Aria both use about half a second.

exports.name: ListMoveOptions
exports.description: `listMove` options.

exports.name: GridMoveOptions
exports.description: `gridMove` options.

exports.name: NavCollection
exports.description: The collection navigation walks: how many items, and which are disabled. Virtual lists answer for unmounted items too.

exports.name: ListIndexOptions
exports.description: `listIndex` options.

exports.name: GridIndexOptions
exports.description: `gridIndex` options. Items fill rows left to right (in reading order), `columns` per row; the last row may be short.

exports.name: TypeaheadOptions
exports.description: `createTypeahead` options.

exports.name: TypeaheadCollection
exports.description: What typeahead searches: the collection plus each item's label.

exports.name: Typeahead
exports.description: Type-to-jump state (K65): one per list.

exports.name: compareItemEquality
exports.description: Compares with `comparer`, except that a missing (`null` or `undefined`) value only equals itself.
exports.signature: <Value>(itemValue: Value, selectedValue: Value, comparer: ItemEquality<Value>) => boolean

exports.name: selectedValueIncludes
exports.description: Whether any of `selectedValues` is `itemValue`.
exports.signature: <Value>(selectedValues: readonly Value[] | null | undefined, itemValue: Value, comparer: ItemEquality<Value>) => boolean

exports.name: findItemIndex
exports.description: The index of the first item value that is `selectedValue`, or -1. Holes (an unregistered index) are skipped.
exports.signature: <Value>(itemValues: readonly (Value | undefined)[] | null | undefined, selectedValue: Value, comparer: ItemEquality<Value>) => number

exports.name: removeItem
exports.description: `selectedValues` without `itemValue`.
exports.signature: <Value>(selectedValues: readonly Value[], itemValue: Value, comparer: ItemEquality<Value>) => Value[]

exports.name: serializeValue
exports.description: A value as the text a form submits: a string as it is, nothing as `""`, anything else as JSON.

exports.name: stringifyAsLabel
exports.description: The text an item value shows: `itemToStringLabel`, else an object's `label` (then its `value`), else the serialised value.
exports.signature: (item: unknown, itemToStringLabel?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => string

exports.name: stringifyAsValue
exports.description: The text a form submits for an item value: `itemToStringValue`, else the `value` of a `{ value, label }` object, else the serialised value.
exports.signature: (item: unknown, itemToStringValue?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => string

exports.name: isGroupedItems
exports.description: True for an array of groups (its first entry has `items`).
exports.signature: (items: readonly unknown[] | null | undefined) => items is readonly ListboxGroup[]

exports.name: flattenListboxItems
exports.description: The entries of an array `items`, groups flattened in order.
exports.signature: <Value, Label>(items: readonly ListboxItem<Value, Label>[] | readonly ListboxGroup<Value, Label>[]) => readonly ListboxItem<Value, Label>[]

exports.name: hasNullItemLabel
exports.description: True when `items` has an entry whose value is `null` or `undefined` and that has a label (the "no choice" option the placeholder is replaced by).

exports.name: hasSelectedValue
exports.description: True when a value counts as chosen: not `null` / `undefined`, not an empty selection, not an empty serialisation.
exports.signature: (value: unknown, multiple: boolean, itemToStringValue?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => boolean

exports.name: resolveSelectedLabel
exports.description:
What the trigger shows for `value`: `itemToStringLabel` first, an object's own `label`, then the label `items` gives it (a record by key, an
array by value), else the value as text. The label of an `items` entry may be any node, so the result is `unknown` here.
exports.signature: (value: unknown, items: ListboxItems | null | undefined, itemToStringLabel?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => unknown

exports.name: resolveMultipleLabels
exports.description: The labels of several values (a multiple select shows them joined), in order.
exports.signature: (values: readonly unknown[], items: ListboxItems | null | undefined, itemToStringLabel?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => unknown[]

exports.name: pickValue
exports.description:
The value after an item is picked. A single list takes the item's value; a multiple list adds it, or removes it when it is already
selected. `selected` is the current value (an array for a multiple list).
exports.signature: <Value>(selected: Value | readonly Value[] | null | undefined, itemValue: Value, options: { readonly multiple: boolean; readonly isSelected: boolean; readonly equal: ItemEquality<Value>; }) => Value | Value[]

exports.name: isValueSelected
exports.description: Whether `itemValue` is selected in `selected` (a list value for a multiple list).
exports.signature: <Value>(selected: Value | readonly Value[] | null | undefined, itemValue: Value, options: { readonly multiple: boolean; readonly equal: ItemEquality<Value>; }) => boolean

exports.name: selectedIndexOf
exports.description: The index (in registration order) a closed list starts its highlight on: the last selected item of a multiple list, the selected item of a single one, else -1.
exports.signature: <Value>(itemValues: readonly (Value | undefined)[], selected: Value | readonly Value[] | null | undefined, options: { readonly multiple: boolean; readonly equal: ItemEquality<Value>; }) => number

exports.name: listboxTriggerKey
exports.description: The arrow key on a closed select's trigger that opens it (APG select-only combobox: Alt+↓ and Alt+↑ open it as well).

exports.name: listboxFocusOnOpen
exports.description:
Where the highlight lands on open. A selected item always (APG: the listbox opens on the selected option, and an aligned popup shows it over
the trigger); with none, the key that opened it says (↓ the first item, ↑ the last), Enter and Space open on the first, and a pointer opens
with nothing highlighted.
exports.signature: (facts: { readonly hasSelected: boolean; readonly key?: "ArrowDown" | "ArrowUp" | null; readonly method: "mouse" | "touch" | "pen" | "keyboard" | null; }) => ListboxFocusOnOpen

exports.name: listboxKeyCommand
exports.description:
The command for `event` in an open list, or null when the list leaves the key alone (Tab and Escape are the layer's, a typed character is the
typeahead's). ↑ and ↓ move, Home and End jump to the ends, PageUp and PageDown jump a page (APG), Enter and Space activate.

exports.name: listboxMoveIndex
exports.description:
The index a move lands on from `current` (-1: nothing highlighted), or null when it stays. With `loopThroughNone` -1 is also an answer:
"back to the input, nothing highlighted".
exports.signature: (move: NavMove, current: number, options: ListboxMoveOptions) => number | null

exports.name: listboxGridMoveIndex
exports.description:
The index a grid move (`left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, the page moves) lands on from `current` (-1: nothing highlighted), or null when it stays. Rows are `columns` items
wide; ← and → stop at a row's ends, ↑ and ↓ keep the column. With `loopThroughNone` ↑ off the first row and ↓ off the last row land on -1 (the input), and from -1 ↓
is the first item and ↑ the last.
exports.signature: (move: NavMove, current: number, options: ListboxGridMoveOptions) => number | null

exports.name: createListboxTypeahead
exports.description: One list's typeahead: `createTypeahead` of the roving maths, so every list searches the same way.

exports.name: releaseChooses
exports.description:
Whether letting go of the pointer button over an item chooses it (press the trigger, drag onto an item, release). The release that ends the
click which opened the list must not choose what lies under it: the unselected items wait 200 ms and the selected one 400 ms (the pointer
is at rest on it when the popup opens aligned), and a list with no selected item waits 400 ms for all of them (Base UI's windows).

exports.name: createListboxFilter
exports.description:
The matchers `Combobox.useFilter` and `Autocomplete.useFilter` hand out: `Intl.Collator` comparison, so "cafe" finds "Café" and "ss" finds "straße"
where the locale says so. One collator per option set is created and kept.

exports.name: createCollatorItemFilter
exports.description: The default filter of a multiple combobox and an autocomplete: `contains` under the collator, over the item's label. A missing item matches nothing.
exports.signature: (filter: ListboxFilter, itemToStringLabel?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => (item: unknown, query: string) => boolean

exports.name: createSingleSelectionFilter
exports.description:
The default filter of a single combobox: everything matches while the query is empty or is exactly the selected item's label (so reopening a filled
combobox shows the whole list, not just the chosen item), else `contains`.
exports.signature: (filter: ListboxFilter, itemToStringLabel: ((item: never) => string) | undefined, selectedValue: unknown) => (item: unknown, query: string) => boolean

exports.name: createComboboxFilter
exports.description: The filter `Combobox.useFilter` returns: `multiple` filters by `contains` alone, a single one by the single-selection rule for `value`.
exports.signature: (options: ListboxFilterOptions & { readonly multiple?: boolean | undefined; readonly value?: unknown; }) => ListboxFilter

exports.name: shouldBypassFiltering
exports.description:
Whether the filter is skipped: a single combobox that has not been typed in since it opened, whose input still reads exactly the selected item's label,
lists everything (the query is the chosen value, not a search).
exports.signature: (facts: { readonly single: boolean; readonly queryChangedAfterOpen: boolean; readonly query: string; readonly selectedLabel: string; readonly filter: ListboxFilter; }) => boolean

exports.name: filterListboxItems
exports.description: `items` kept by `query`: a flat array filtered, a group array filtered per group with empty groups dropped. An empty query keeps everything (up to `limit`).
exports.signature: <Item>(items: readonly Item[], query: string, options: FilterListboxItemsOptions) => readonly Item[]

exports.name: listboxInputKeyCommand
exports.description:
The command for `event` on a combobox input, or null when the input keeps the key (typing, the caret keys: Home and End stay the caret's, Escape is the
layer's, Tab leaves). ↓ and ↑ open a closed list and move through an open one, PageDown and PageUp jump a page, Enter chooses the highlighted item. Ctrl, Meta and
Shift keys are the input's; Alt+↓ opens without moving the highlight.

exports.name: chipInputKeyCommand
exports.description: The chip command for `event` on the input: ← (→ in RTL) at the start of the text goes to the last chip, Backspace on an empty input removes it.

exports.name: chipFocusAfterRemoval
exports.description: The chip that is focused after `index` of `count` chips is removed: the one that took its place, else the one before it, else the input (null).

exports.name: chipKeyCommand
exports.description:
The command for `event` on the chip at `context.index`: ← and → move between chips (mirrored in RTL), past either end focus returns to the input; Backspace and Delete
remove it; ↓ and ↑ open the list; Enter, Space and a printable character return to the input.

exports.name: autocompleteModeFlags
exports.description:
What a mode means: `inline` is whether the input temporarily shows the highlighted item (inline completion), `filtered` whether the list is narrowed by what
was typed (`list` and `both`; `inline` and `none` list everything).
exports.signature: (mode: AutocompleteMode) => { readonly inline: boolean; readonly filtered: boolean; }

exports.name: inlineCompletionText
exports.description: The text the input shows for a highlighted item of an inline autocomplete: its label, or nothing when nothing is highlighted (the typed text comes back).
exports.signature: (highlightedValue: unknown, itemToStringValue?: ((item: never) => string) | undefined) => string

exports.name: ItemEquality
exports.description: Whether an item's value is the selected one.

exports.name: defaultItemEquality
exports.description: `Object.is`: object values that are not the same reference need `isItemEqualToValue`.

exports.name: ListboxItem
exports.description: One entry of `items`: the value an option carries and what it shows.

exports.name: ListboxGroup
exports.description: A labelled group of entries (`Select.Group`).

exports.name: ListboxItems
exports.description: What `items` may be: a record from value to label, entries, or groups of entries.

exports.name: ListboxFocusOnOpen
exports.description: Where the highlight lands when a list opens: on the selected item, on an end, or nowhere (the popup holds focus and the next arrow key starts at an end).

exports.name: ListboxKeyCommand
exports.description: What a key does in an open list. `move` goes through the roving maths; the rest are listbox rules.

exports.name: ListboxKeyContext
exports.description: What `listboxKeyCommand` needs besides the key: the text direction and whether Space activates.

exports.name: ListboxMoveOptions
exports.description: Options for `listboxMoveIndex`: the item count, wrapping and how disabled items are skipped.

exports.name: ListboxGridMoveOptions
exports.description: Options for `listboxGridMoveIndex`: a list laid out in rows of `columns` items.

exports.name: LISTBOX_UNSELECTED_RELEASE_DELAY_MS
exports.description: A press on a select's trigger let go over an item before this long (ms) is a click on the trigger, not a choice, when an item was already selected.

exports.name: LISTBOX_SELECTED_RELEASE_DELAY_MS
exports.description: The same for the selected item itself, which the pointer rests on when the list opens aligned over the trigger.

exports.name: ListboxReleaseFacts
exports.description: What `releaseChooses` needs to tell a press-drag-release choice from a click on the trigger.

exports.name: ListboxFilterOptions
exports.description: What `createListboxFilter` takes: `Intl.Collator`'s options and a locale. Defaults: `usage: "search"`, `sensitivity: "base"`, `ignorePunctuation: true`.

exports.name: ListboxFilter
exports.description: The matchers of one collator. Each takes an item, the query and `itemToString` (else the item's label as `stringifyAsLabel` reads it). An empty query matches everything.

exports.name: ListboxItemFilter
exports.description: A filter as a combobox takes it: does this item match the query. `itemToString` is the root's `itemToStringLabel`.

exports.name: FilterListboxItemsOptions
exports.description: Options for `filterListboxItems`: the filter, how an item becomes a label and how many items to keep.

exports.name: ListboxInputCommand
exports.description: What a key does on a combobox's text input.

exports.name: ListboxInputKeyContext
exports.description: What `listboxInputKeyCommand` needs besides the key: the list's open and highlight state.

exports.name: ChipInputCommand
exports.description: What a key does on the input when the combobox has chips. `index` is the chip to focus (the last one's, from the input's start).

exports.name: ChipInputKeyContext
exports.description: What `chipInputKeyCommand` needs besides the key: how many chips there are and where the input's caret is.

exports.name: ChipCommand
exports.description: What a key does on a focused chip. `next` is the chip that gets focus after (null: the input).

exports.name: ChipKeyContext
exports.description: What `chipKeyCommand` needs besides the key: the focused chip, the chip count and the text direction.

exports.name: AutocompleteMode
exports.description: How an autocomplete lists and completes (Base UI's `Autocomplete.Root` `mode`).

exports.name: scrollArrowVisibility
exports.description: Which scroll arrows show: ▲ once scrolled off the start, ▼ while there is more below.
exports.signature: (scrollTop: number, scrollHeight: number, clientHeight: number) => { readonly up: boolean; readonly down: boolean; }

exports.name: planSelectAlignment
exports.description:
The first pass of `alignItemWithTrigger`. The popup's top is where the selected item's text centre lands on the value's centre; its bottom is the
viewport's bottom edge (less the margins), so its ideal height is the room from there down. A popup taller than the viewport is cut to it and
the rest becomes the scroll offset.

exports.name: finishSelectAlignment
exports.description:
The second pass, once the plan's height is applied and the scroller's real `maxScrollTop` is known. A list taller than the room is pinned to the
viewport's bottom with the scroll offset that shows the selected item over the trigger; a list that fits is pinned by its top edge. A trigger
too near the top or bottom of the viewport, a list that would be squeezed below `minHeight`, or a pinch-zoomed Safari give up (`fallback`).

exports.name: growOnScroll
exports.description:
An aligned popup that was cut short by the viewport grows as the list is scrolled toward the cut edge, so scrolling consumes the viewport's
room before it scrolls the content: what the scroll offset says is still hidden becomes height, up to `maxAvailableHeight`.

exports.name: scrollArrowTarget
exports.description:
The scroll offset one step of a held scroll arrow goes to: ▲ reveals the item just above the first fully visible one, ▼ the item just below
the last fully visible one, so the list moves item by item rather than by pixel. At the end it goes to the end.
exports.signature: (items: readonly ScrollArrowItem[], up: boolean, scrollTop: number, clientHeight: number, arrowHeight: number, maxScrollTop: number) => number

exports.name: SCROLL_EDGE_TOLERANCE_PX
exports.description: A scroll offset within this many px of an edge counts as AT the edge (sub-pixel scrolling and rounding).

exports.name: SelectRect
exports.description: A rectangle in viewport pixels.

exports.name: SELECT_TRIGGER_COLLISION_PX
exports.description: How far from the viewport's top or bottom the trigger may be before the popup stops overlaying it (a popup that cannot grow either way is useless).

exports.name: SELECT_EDGE_PADDING_PX
exports.description: The popup keeps this far from the viewport's left and right edges.

exports.name: SELECT_DEFAULT_MARGIN_PX
exports.description: The margins the positioner falls back to when its style gives none.

exports.name: SELECT_DEFAULT_MIN_HEIGHT_PX
exports.description: The smallest height an aligned popup may have before the layout falls back to the plain, anchored placement.

exports.name: SelectAlignInput
exports.description: What `planSelectAlignment` measures: the trigger, positioner, value and text boxes, the viewport and the margins.

exports.name: SelectAlignPlan
exports.description: The first pass: where the popup goes sideways, and how tall it would be to reach the viewport's bottom edge from the selected item's row.

exports.name: SelectAlignFinishInput
exports.description: What `finishSelectAlignment` needs on top of the first pass: the plan and the scroller's real measurements.

exports.name: SelectAlignment
exports.description: The layout the DOM writes, or the order to give up and place the popup against the trigger instead.

exports.name: SelectGrowInput
exports.description: What `growOnScroll` needs: the positioner's height, how far it may grow, the scroll offsets and which edge it is pinned by.

exports.name: SelectGrow
exports.description: What `growOnScroll` changes: the new height and scroll offset, each only when it changes.

exports.name: SCROLL_ARROW_INTERVAL_MS
exports.description: How often a held scroll arrow steps to the next item (ms).

exports.name: ScrollArrowItem
exports.description: An item's vertical extent inside the scroller.

exports.name: toastLayoutOf
exports.description: Position of every toast: its index in the list, its index among the ones not closing, and the sum of the heights before it.

exports.name: toastIndexVariable
exports.description: The value of `--toast-index`: a closing toast keeps its list index (it leaves from where it was), the others count the visible ones.

exports.name: nextToastToFocus
exports.description: The toast focus moves to when the one at `id` closes: the next one in the list that is not closing, else the previous one; undefined when none is left.
exports.signature: (toasts: readonly ToastFields[], id: string) => ToastFields | undefined

exports.name: resolveToastPromiseOption
exports.description: A promise toast's option: a string is the description, a function is called with the settled value.
exports.signature: <Arg, T extends ToastFields>(option: ToastPromiseOption<Arg, T> | string | ToastUpdateOptions<T>, arg?: Arg) => ToastUpdateOptions<T>

exports.name: createToastStore
exports.description: Creates a toast store with no toasts.

exports.name: TOAST_PRIORITIES
exports.description: How urgently a toast is announced: `low` politely (the viewport is a polite live region), `high` urgently (an `alertdialog` and an `alert` announcement).

exports.name: ToastPriority
exports.description: One of `TOAST_PRIORITIES`.

exports.name: TOAST_CLOSE_REASONS
exports.description: Why a toast closed: its clock ran out, the user closed it (the × button, an action), swiped it, pressed Escape, code closed it, or a full group dropped it.

exports.name: ToastCloseReason
exports.description: One of `TOAST_CLOSE_REASONS`.

exports.name: ToastCloseDetails
exports.description: What a toast's `onClose` receives: why it closed and the toast as it was.

exports.name: ToastTransitionStatus
exports.description: `starting` for the first frame of an enter, `ending` while the toast animates out (then it is removed).

exports.name: TOAST_OVERFLOW_POLICIES
exports.description: What happens when a group already shows `limit` toasts (see the file comment).

exports.name: ToastOverflowPolicy
exports.description: One of `TOAST_OVERFLOW_POLICIES`.

exports.name: TOAST_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS
exports.description: The default time a toast stays up, ms (Base UI's `timeout`).

exports.name: TOAST_DEFAULT_LIMIT
exports.description: The default number of toasts shown at once (Base UI's `limit`).

exports.name: ToastFields
exports.description: The fields the store itself writes and reads on every toast. A host's own fields ride along on the record.

exports.name: ToastManagedKey
exports.description: The keys the store manages itself: a caller cannot pass them to `add` or `update`.

exports.name: ToastAddOptions
exports.description: What a caller passes to `add`: every field but the managed ones, all optional.

exports.name: ToastUpdateOptions
exports.description: What `update` accepts: a partial toast without its id and the managed fields.

exports.name: ToastClock
exports.description: The timer seam, so tests (and a host with its own scheduler) drive time.

exports.name: ToastFocusHost
exports.description: Where focus goes when the toast that holds it closes: the store decides which toast, the host moves focus.

exports.name: ToastStoreOptions
exports.description: Options for `createToastStore`.

exports.name: ToastStoreState
exports.description: What a viewer sees: the toasts newest first and the pointer and focus state around them.

props.name: toasts
props.description: The toasts, newest first.

props.name: hovering
props.description: Whether the pointer is over the toast viewport.

props.name: focused
props.description: Whether focus is inside the toast viewport.

props.name: windowFocused
props.description: False while the browser window has lost focus (clocks stop, so nobody misses a toast).

props.name: expanded
props.description: Hovered or focused: the stack lays out in full.

props.name: paused
props.description: A clock is stopped: hovered, focused, window blurred, or a pause reason is held.

exports.name: ToastLayoutEntry
exports.description: One toast's place in the list, for the `--toast-index` and `--toast-offset-y` variables.

exports.name: ToastPromiseOption
exports.description: The two messages of a promise toast: text (the description), or options, or a function of the result.

exports.name: ToastPromiseOptions
exports.description: The messages of a promise toast: while it runs, when it resolves and when it rejects.

exports.name: ToastStore
exports.description: The toast store: the queue of toasts, their timers and the viewer state a renderer subscribes to.

exports.name: createToastManager
exports.description: Creates a toast manager: one per app (or per provider), imported wherever a toast is raised.

exports.name: ToastManagerEvent
exports.description: One event a toast manager emits to its provider: the call that was made and its options.

exports.name: ToastManager
exports.description: A toast manager: raises, updates and closes toasts from code outside React through the `Toast.Provider` it is given to.

exports.name: toastStackLayout
exports.description: Lays out one group's stack: one slot per toast, newest first, collapsed or expanded.
exports.signature: ({ heights, expanded, gap, peek, visible }: ToastStackInput) => ToastStackLayout

exports.name: TOAST_STACK_PEEK_PX
exports.description: Pixels each older toast peeks out behind the front one while collapsed.

exports.name: TOAST_STACK_GAP_PX
exports.description: Gap between toasts while expanded.

exports.name: TOAST_STACK_SCALE_STEP
exports.description: How much smaller each older toast is drawn while collapsed (5% per step).

exports.name: TOAST_STACK_VISIBLE
exports.description: Older toasts that peek out while collapsed; the rest are hidden but stay mounted.

exports.name: ToastStackInput
exports.description: What `toastStackLayout` needs: the measured heights, whether the stack is expanded, and optional spacing.

exports.name: ToastStackSlot
exports.description: Where one toast in the stack sits and how it is drawn.

props.name: offset
props.description: Distance from the stack's edge (bottom for bottom positions, top for top), px.

props.name: scale
props.description: The scale the toast is drawn at (1 in front or expanded).

props.name: opacity
props.description: The toast's opacity, 0 to 1.

props.name: height
props.description: Height the toast is drawn at: its own when expanded or in front, the front toast's while peeking.

props.name: zIndex
props.description: Paint order: the front toast paints on top.

props.name: hidden
props.description: Out of the visible window: not focusable and not hit-testable.

exports.name: ToastStackLayout
exports.description: The result of `toastStackLayout`: one slot per toast and the stack's height.

exports.name: toastSwipeOutcome
exports.description: Whether a finished swipe dismisses the toast: a mostly vertical drag cancels; otherwise distance or speed decides.
exports.signature: ({ dx, dy, elapsedMs, width }: ToastSwipeSample) => ToastSwipeOutcome

exports.name: toastSwipeOutcomeBySpeed
exports.description:
The same rule when the gesture reports its own average speed (px per ms) instead of a duration, as the shared swipe gesture's release does
(`SwipeReleaseInfo.velocityX`), and has already kept a mostly vertical drag from counting.
exports.signature: ({ dx, speed, width }: { readonly dx: number; readonly speed: number; readonly width: number; }) => ToastSwipeOutcome

exports.name: toastSwipeOpacity
exports.description: Opacity while dragging: fades out as the toast nears the dismiss distance.

exports.name: TOAST_SWIPE_DISTANCE_RATIO
exports.description: Fraction of the toast's width a slow drag must cover to dismiss.

exports.name: TOAST_SWIPE_VELOCITY
exports.description: A flick faster than this (px per ms) dismisses even when short.

exports.name: TOAST_SWIPE_MIN_PX
exports.description: A flick must still travel this far, so a tap with jitter never dismisses.

exports.name: TOAST_SWIPE_OUTCOMES
exports.description: What a lateral swipe on a toast ends in: `dismiss` or `cancel`.

exports.name: ToastSwipeOutcome
exports.description: One of `TOAST_SWIPE_OUTCOMES`.

exports.name: ToastSwipeSample
exports.description: A finished swipe on a toast: its travel, its duration and the toast's width.

exports.name: attachLayerDom
exports.description:
Wires one layer of `layers` (which must already hold it) to the DOM: its regions, its handlers and the
shared document listeners. Returns the unregister. Does not add the layer to the model: whoever owns
the layer does (the overlay stack for its entries, `useDismissLayer` for a standalone part).
exports.signature: (layers: DismissLayers<string>, id: string, registration: LayerRegistration) => () => void

exports.name: isEventInsideLayer
exports.description: Did `event` pass through the popup of layer `id` or of a layer nested in it, in the React tree? (After React's capture handlers ran: see `afterCapture`.)
exports.signature: (layers: DismissLayers<string>, id: string, event: Event) => boolean

exports.name: isInsideLayer
exports.description:
Is `target` inside layer `id`: in its own regions or in the regions of any layer nested in it? This is
the "inside this layer?" decision, public so a part can ask it for its own events (a focus-out, a
pointer-up) with the same rule the press listener uses.
exports.signature: (layers: DismissLayers<string>, id: string, target: Node | null) => boolean

exports.name: LayerRegistration
exports.description: What a layer gives the dispatcher. All optional: a layer may only want to mark regions.

exports.name: closeWatcherSupported
exports.description:
Does a close request reach this window through a `CloseWatcher`? True on Android where the constructor exists (Chromium 120 and up).
Everywhere else the close request is Escape (the dismiss layers listen to it) or there is none, and nothing here is created.

exports.name: createCloseWatcher
exports.description:
Creates a close watcher on `win` that calls `onClose` with the `close` event. Returns what destroys it, or `null` when the platform has
none (see `closeWatcherSupported`) or refused to create one (a window that is not fully active). The browser destroys a watcher when it
fires, so a layer that stays open after a request creates a new one.
exports.signature: (win: Window, onClose: (event: Event) => void) => (() => void) | null

exports.name: isAndroid
exports.description: Is `win` an Android browser? Read from the user agent, as Base UI does.

exports.name: activeElementTarget
exports.description: The element focused right now (the implicit opener when no trigger is known), or null on the server or when nothing is focused.

exports.name: BODY_FOCUS_TARGET
exports.description: A walk's last stop. Resolved lazily so a stack created during SSR never touches `document`.

exports.name: deepActiveElement
exports.description: The focused element, looking through open shadow roots (a shadow host reports itself as active).

exports.name: elementTarget
exports.description:
Wraps one element as somewhere focus can go. Unavailable once it left the document (row deleted, menu
unmounted), is disabled or sits under `inert`, so a walk over several candidates moves on to the next.

exports.name: focusLeftBehind
exports.description:
May a closing layer move focus back to where it came from? Only when focus is still "left behind":
on nothing or the body (the content unmounted under it), or inside the closing content itself. When
the user has moved on (a non-modal panel closed by code while they type in the page) focus is theirs
and stays. `alsoLeftBehind` lets an owner add its own case, e.g. focus inside a sibling layer that is
closing too (the overlay stack passes "inside a layer that is no longer live").
exports.signature: (content: HTMLElement | null, alsoLeftBehind?: (active: Element) => boolean) => boolean

exports.name: createFocusGuard
exports.description: Creates one guard in `doc`. `onFocus` runs when focus lands on it; `relatedTarget` is where focus came from.

exports.name: FOCUS_GUARD_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: The marker attribute every focus guard carries, so other code can recognise it.

exports.name: FOCUS_GUARD_STYLE
exports.description: Visually hidden, still focusable (`display:none` would not take focus).

exports.name: isFocusGuard
exports.description: True when `el` is a focus guard of any region.

exports.name: trapFocus
exports.description: Starts a trap and focuses inside it.

exports.name: FocusTrap
exports.description: A running focus trap, returned by `trapFocus`.

exports.name: FocusTrapOptions
exports.description: Options for `trapFocus`: the container, whether Tab wraps, and where focus goes at the start and at the end.

exports.name: InitialFocus
exports.description: What the trap focuses when it starts: nothing (`false`), an element, or a function that picks one (null or `true` means the default).

exports.name: ReturnFocus
exports.description: Where focus goes when the trap is released: nothing (`false`), an element or target, or a function that picks one (null or undefined means the default, `false` means nothing).

exports.name: inertOutside
exports.description:
Make every element outside `inside` inert, from `inside` up to its document's body, crossing shadow
roots to their hosts. Returns the undo.

exports.name: InertOutsideOptions
exports.description: Options for `inertOutside`.

exports.name: UndoInert
exports.description: Restores what `inertOutside` changed. Call once.

exports.name: isPortalHost
exports.description: True for an element that hosts the portals of a scope.

exports.name: PORTAL_HOST_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: Marks an element that hosts the portals of a scope (`PortalHost`): a portal node appended into it takes no layout box of its own.

exports.name: portalHostOf
exports.description:
The host of the nearest scope that contains `element`: the host is the last child of the element its `PortalHost` was rendered in, so
the walk looks at the last child of each ancestor. Null when no scope contains it.

exports.name: resolvePortalContainer
exports.description: The node a portal appends into, or null on the server (no document).

exports.name: resolvePortalPlacement
exports.description:
Where a portal goes. Precedence: the container the portal's own props name, then the scope that contains `near`, then the nearest
scope's (`PortalContainerProvider`), then `document.body`. A scope whose container does not exist yet holds its portals back: the
result is null until it does, so a popup that opens in the first render does not mount in the body and then jump into the scope.

exports.name: resolvePortalTarget
exports.description: {@link resolvePortalPlacement}'s target only.
exports.signature: (own: PortalContainerOption, inherited: PortalContainerOption, doc?: Document) => PortalContainer | null

exports.name: PortalContainer
exports.description: A portal target: an element (any document's) or a shadow root.

exports.name: PortalContainerOption
exports.description: What a host may pass: a container, a function that returns one (called when the portal mounts), or nothing for `document.body`.

exports.name: PortalPlacement
exports.description: Where a portal went and why: the portal's own `container` ("own"), a scope's ("scope"), or the document body ("body").

exports.name: PortalPlacementOptions
exports.description: What `resolvePortalPlacement` chooses from: the portal's own container and the one its nearest scope names.

exports.name: capturePagePortals
exports.description: Records the nodes that are the page right now.

exports.name: isInLaterPortal
exports.description:
Is `node` under a top-level body node that was not there when `pages` was taken? Crosses shadow roots to their
hosts. A node outside the body, or with no snapshot, is not in a later portal.

exports.name: PagePortals
exports.description: The top-level body nodes at one moment.

exports.name: insidePopupTree
exports.description:
True when `target` is inside any popup of the tree `tree`. Compares attribute values instead of building a
selector from the id: no escaping to get wrong, and no `CSS.escape` (an engine without a `CSS` global, such as
jsdom, would throw on every press).

exports.name: POPUP_TREE_ATTR
exports.description: The attribute every popup of one tree carries; nested popups (submenus) share the value.

exports.name: isIOS
exports.description: True on iPhone, iPad (including iPadOS, which reports as a Mac with touch) and iPod.

exports.name: lockScroll
exports.description:
Locks the page scroll of the document `reference` belongs to (default: the global document) and
returns the release. Each call is one hold: the page stays locked until every hold is released.

exports.name: SCROLL_LOCK_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: Set on <html> while the lock is applied: a hook for CSS and for tests.

exports.name: scrollLockCount
exports.description: How many holds the document has right now (the lock is applied while this is above 0, or until the pending unlock runs).

exports.name: bridgeTabOrder
exports.description:
Starts bridging; returns the stop. `marker` is where the portal sits in the React tree, `portal` the node its content lives in. A bridge
stands down while focus is inside a bridged region nested in its own: that region's own bridge decides (the innermost one acts).
exports.signature: (marker: Element, portal: Element, options?: BridgeTabOrderOptions) => () => void

exports.name: BridgeTabOrderOptions
exports.description: Options for `bridgeTabOrder`.

exports.name: adjacentTabbable
exports.description:
The tab stop after (`backwards` false) or before `from` in its document, skipping stops `skip` rejects.
Wraps at the ends by default (null only when nothing else is a stop); with `wrap` false it stops at
the ends and answers null there, which is what "is there a stop between here and the edge" needs.
exports.signature: (from: Element, backwards: boolean, skip?: (el: HTMLElement) => boolean, wrap?: boolean) => HTMLElement | null

exports.name: composedContains
exports.description: Like `container.contains(node)` but looking through shadow roots: a node inside a shadow root inside `container` is contained.

exports.name: focusables
exports.description: Every focusable element under `root` in DOM order, open shadow roots and slots followed. `root` itself is not included.

exports.name: isFocusable
exports.description: True when `el` can take focus from a script or a click (tabindex -1 included), not necessarily from Tab.

exports.name: isTabbable
exports.description: True when Tab stops on `el`: focusable, `tabindex >= 0`, and not a radio its group skips.

exports.name: tabbables
exports.description:
Every tab stop under `root` in the order Tab visits them: positive `tabindex` ascending first, then the
zeros in DOM order. Open shadow roots and slots are followed, closed shadow roots cannot be. `root`
itself is not included.

exports.name: bindSwipe
exports.description:
Wires `gesture` to `viewport`. Mouse and pen: pointer events (a press that starts in marked content or on
a swipe-ignored element never swipes). Touch: touch events, with Base UI's scroll arbitration: a touch that
starts on a scroll container swipes only when the container sits at the edge the swipe starts from and the
finger moves toward dismissal; a mostly-across touch keeps its native cross-axis scroll; range inputs and
pinch gestures are left alone; and a non-passive `touchmove` on the document stops the page behind from
scrolling.

exports.name: createSwipeGesture
exports.description: Creates one gesture. See the file header.

exports.name: elementTransform
exports.description: The element's current translate and scale, read from its computed transform.
exports.signature: (element: HTMLElement) => { x: number; y: number; scale: number; }

exports.name: DRAWER_CONTENT_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: Marks the drawer's scrolling content: a MOUSE press that starts in it never swipes (it selects text, drags a scrollbar). Touch handles scroll containers on its own.

exports.name: elementAtPoint
exports.description: The topmost element at a viewport point, or null (an engine with no layout has none).
exports.signature: (doc: Document, x: number, y: number) => Element | null

exports.name: findScrollableTouchTarget
exports.description: The nearest scrollable element from `target` up to `root` on `axis`, or `root` itself when it scrolls, else null.
exports.signature: (target: Element | null, root: Element, axis: "vertical" | "horizontal") => HTMLElement | null

exports.name: ignoreSwipeForTextSelection
exports.description: True when a text field in the popup has a selected range, or a page selection touches the root: a touch then adjusts the selection and must not swipe.

exports.name: isSwipeIgnoredTarget
exports.description: True when `target` is inside an element marked `data-base-ui-swipe-ignore`.

exports.name: registerSwipeCssProperties
exports.description: Registers the swipe CSS variables as non-inheriting (`CSS.registerProperty`), once per page; a no-op where the API is missing.

exports.name: SWIPE_IGNORE_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: The marker that makes a pointer-down inside never start a swipe (a resize grip, a range input's wrapper). Base UI's name, kept.

exports.name: BindSwipeOptions
exports.description: Options for `bindSwipe`: the viewport to listen on and the gesture to drive.

exports.name: SwipeBinding
exports.description: A swipe gesture bound to a viewport by `bindSwipe`.

exports.name: SwipeGesture
exports.description: A swipe gesture: the event handlers `bindSwipe` calls, and the current snapshot.

exports.name: SwipeGestureOptions
exports.description: Options for `createSwipeGesture`: the popup, the directions, the thresholds and the callbacks.

exports.name: SwipeInput
exports.description: One pointer or touch event as the swipe gesture reads it.

exports.name: SwipeOffset
exports.description: A 2D offset in px.

exports.name: SwipeProgressDetails
exports.description: What `onProgress` receives while the drag moves: the movement so far and the direction it committed to.

exports.name: SwipeReleaseInfo
exports.description: What `onRelease` receives when the pointer is let go: the event, the direction, the travel and the speeds.

exports.name: SwipeSnapshot
exports.description: What the gesture shows the world: enough to write the drawer's CSS variables and `data-swiping`.

exports.name: anchoredAttributes
exports.description: The state attributes of a positioner, as plain attributes (React callers spread `anchoredAttributes` instead).
exports.signature: (result: Pick<AnchoredPositionResult, "dataSide" | "align" | "anchorHidden">) => { readonly "data-side": string; readonly "data-align": string; readonly "data-anchor-hidden"?: ""; }

exports.name: anchoredStyle
exports.description: The inline style that puts the popup where `measureAnchored` placed it: a `translate` from 0,0, or `left`/`top` from the far edge when `adaptive`.
exports.signature: (result: Pick<AnchoredDomResult, "x" | "y" | "strategy" | "devicePixelRatio"> & { readonly origin?: AdaptiveOrigin; }, adaptive?: boolean) => AnchoredStyle

exports.name: measureAnchored
exports.description:
Measures `anchor` and `floating` and computes where the popup goes. Writes `--available-width` and
`--available-height` on the popup while it does (a popup styled `max-height: var(--available-height)` is laid out again
and measured at the size it will have); the caller applies the result with `anchoredStyle`,
`writeAnchoredVariables` and `writeAnchoredAttributes`.
exports.signature: (anchor: AnchorTarget, floating: HTMLElement, options?: AnchoredDomOptions) => AnchoredDomResult

exports.name: writeAnchoredAttributes
exports.description: Writes `anchoredAttributes` onto an element, removing `data-anchor-hidden` when the anchor is visible again.

exports.name: writeAnchoredVariables
exports.description: The CSS variables a popup's styles read: the room it has, the anchor's size and the origin its scale animations grow from.

exports.name: AnchoredDomOptions
exports.description: Options for `measureAnchored`: the core placement options, with the boxes and boundaries read from the DOM instead of passed in.

exports.name: AnchoredDomResult
exports.description: A measured position: the maths' result plus how the popup was placed.

exports.name: AnchoredStyle
exports.description: The inline style that puts the popup where `measureAnchored` said (`translate`, so a move never relayouts; with `adaptiveOrigin`, `left` / `right` and `top` / `bottom` instead).

exports.name: CollisionBoundary
exports.description: Where the popup may not leave: its clipping ancestors (default), one element's box, several, or a rectangle in viewport pixels.

exports.name: PositionStrategy
exports.description: The CSS `position` the popup is placed with: `absolute` against its offset parent, or `fixed` against the viewport.

exports.name: anchorElement
exports.description: The element behind an anchor (the anchor itself, or a virtual anchor's context), or null.

exports.name: autoUpdate
exports.description:
Calls `update` now and on every change that can move either box, at most once per animation frame.
Environments without `ResizeObserver` or `IntersectionObserver` (jsdom) skip those two sources.
exports.signature: (anchor: AnchorTarget, floating: HTMLElement, update: () => void, options?: AutoUpdateOptions) => Cleanup

exports.name: composedParent
exports.description: Parent in the composed tree: through a slot to its host's tree and out of a shadow root to its host.

exports.name: isOverflowElement
exports.description: True for an element whose own scrollbars or clipping apply to its descendants.

exports.name: overflowAncestors
exports.description: Every ancestor of `node` (composed tree) that clips or scrolls, nearest first, ending with the window.

exports.name: AnchorTarget
exports.description: What a popup can be anchored to: an element or a virtual anchor.

exports.name: AutoUpdateOptions
exports.description: Which changes `autoUpdate` follows; each is on unless turned off.

exports.name: VirtualAnchor
exports.description: What an anchor may be: an element, or a virtual anchor (a pointer position) that names the element it belongs to.

exports.name: ANCHOR_HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: The state attribute on a positioner while its anchor is clipped away (Base UI writes it from Floating UI's `hide`; `useAnchored` writes it from `computeAnchoredPosition`).

exports.name: cssAnchorPositioner
exports.description:
EXPERIMENTAL engine (D4): CSS anchor positioning. The browser places the
popup (`position-area`), flips it when it does not fit
(`position-try-fallbacks`) and follows the anchor every frame with no
script, which is the whole appeal for moving anchors (O36). Hidden-anchor
detection uses an IntersectionObserver on the anchor, so `whenAnchorHidden`
behaves as with the default engine. Limits: no shift-into-view on the
alignment axis (only flips), and an anchor inside a different containing
block than the popup is invisible to CSS; that is why it is opt-in.

exports.name: DEFAULT_PLACEMENT
exports.description: Popover default: below, centred, a 4px gap (the `@/components/ui/popover` look).

exports.name: effectivePositioner
exports.description: The engine a surface actually runs: the requested one when the browser supports it, else the default.

exports.name: floatingUiPositioner
exports.description:
The default engine: Base UI's Positioner (Floating UI inside) does the
placement; this only relays its `data-anchor-hidden` state.

exports.name: supportsCssAnchorPositioning
exports.description: True when the browser implements the parts of CSS anchor positioning this engine relies on.

exports.name: Cleanup
exports.description: Undoes what an engine set up (listeners, CSS properties).

exports.name: FloatingStyle
exports.description:
The inline style an engine layers over the popup's positioner element. It names only the properties an
engine writes, with value types React's `CSSProperties` also accepts, so a result spreads straight into a
`style` prop without this layer importing React.

exports.name: Positioner
exports.description: A positioning engine: places a popup's positioner element against its anchor, in place of the default Floating UI placement.

exports.name: PositionerAlign
exports.description: Alignment along the anchor's edge (the same three as `AnchoredAlign`).

exports.name: PositionerPlacement
exports.description: Where an engine places the popup: the side, the alignment and the gap.

exports.name: PositionerSide
exports.description: Physical side of the anchor the popup sits on (the same four sides as `AnchoredSide`).

exports.name: createFocusIntent
exports.description: Creates the focus intent for one popup, following the rules at the top of this file.

exports.name: FocusIntent
exports.description: Focus intent for focus-opened popups (tooltip, preview card): opens on visible focus, closes on blur.

exports.name: FocusIntentOptions
exports.description: What `createFocusIntent` reads (the open state, the delay, the popup) and how it opens and closes the popup.

exports.name: matchesFocusVisible
exports.description:
Whether `element` matches `:focus-visible` as the focus-opened popups (tooltip, preview card) read it: a pointer press that focuses the
trigger must not open a tooltip, a keyboard arrival must. jsdom matches `:focus-visible` only without `:focus`
and a browser too old for the selector throws; both count as visible, so a test environment behaves like the
keyboard case. No element counts as visible too.

exports.name: createHoverTargets
exports.description: Creates the hover listeners for one popup: mouse events become hover-intent calls, and the safe polygon decides a leave on the way into the popup.

exports.name: HoverTargets
exports.description: The DOM half of hover intent: listens on the trigger and the popup and feeds the core state machine.

exports.name: RequiredProxy
exports.description:
`required` for a control that is not a native input: an invisible required text input whose value says whether the
control is filled. A plain form's submit is refused while it is empty, and the browser's `invalid` event moves focus
to the control (`focusTarget`) instead of the invisible proxy: the event is cancelled, so the browser neither focuses
the proxy nor anchors its message to it (an enclosing `Field`'s error says what is missing).

Inside a primitives (or ui) `Field` it also is the Field's validation input, required or not, as the hidden input of a
Checkbox or a Select is: the Field reads its validity (`valueMissing` while required and empty, else valid), so a
`Form` submits a kit control's Field and refuses an empty required one. Outside a Field it renders only while required.

props.description: The `form` the proxy belongs to.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled control is never required.

props.name: data-slot
props.description: Extra attributes for the proxy (a `data-slot` for styling hooks and tests).

exports.name: useFieldControl
exports.description:
A kit control's part in an enclosing `Field`: its id is the one the Field's label points at, the Field's
description and error describe it, the Field's `disabled`, `invalid` and `name` reach it, and it is registered with the
Field and the `Form` (`useRegisterFieldControl`) so a `Form` reads its value and focuses it on a refused submit. Pair it
with `HiddenInputs` (posting) and `RequiredProxy` (`required`, and the Field's validation input). Outside a Field it
hands back the control's own props unchanged.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is open (controlled).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the dialog starts open (uncontrolled).

props.name: modal
props.description:
`true` (default): focus is trapped, the page scroll is locked, everything outside is inert. `false`: the page
stays usable and moving focus out dismisses. `"trap-focus"`: focus is trapped but the page stays scrollable and clickable.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the dialog asks to open or close. Call `details.cancel()` to refuse.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Called after the enter animation finished (`true`) or the exit animation finished and the popup unmounted (`false`).

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: An outside press (and focus leaving a non-modal dialog) does not dismiss. Escape still does.

props.name: layerId
props.description:
Kitora extension: adopt this layer of the dismiss-layer model instead of registering a new one. An
overlay entry's id, so the entry and its surface are ONE layer and the stack stays the owner of which
gesture goes where. A layer the model does not hold yet is added as usual.

props.name: keepInteractive
props.description:
Kitora extension: a CSS selector for regions that stay interactive while a modal is open, on top of live
regions (`[aria-live]`): a persistent toast region, a host's chat widget. Everything else outside is `inert`.

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger the dialog is attached to: with a controlled `open`, which of several triggers it opens from.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger the dialog is attached to when it starts open (`defaultOpen`).

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions: `close()`, and `unmount()` for a popup kept mounted with `details.preventUnmountOnClose()`.

props.name: handle
props.description: A handle that lets triggers outside this Root open it (`Dialog.createHandle()`).

props.name: children
props.description: The content: nodes, or a function of the `payload` of the trigger the dialog is attached to.

parts.name: Backdrop
parts.description: An overlay displayed beneath the popup. Renders a `<div>`.

props.name: forceRender
props.description: Render the backdrop of a nested dialog too (by default only the outermost one draws one).

parts.name: Close
parts.description: A button that closes the dialog. Renders a `<button>`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the button does nothing.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Set to `false` when `render` is not a native `<button>`.

parts.name: Description
parts.description:
A paragraph with more about the dialog (its `aria-describedby`). Renders a `

`.

parts.name: Popup
parts.description: A container for the dialog contents. Renders a `<div>`.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
What to focus when the dialog opens: `false` nothing; `true` the first tab stop; an element (a ref); or a
function of how it was opened that returns an element, `true` for the default, or `false` for nothing.
Default: the popup itself when opened by touch (no on-screen keyboard), else the first tab stop.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description:
Where focus goes when the dialog closes: `false` nowhere; an element (a ref); or a function of how it
closed that returns an element, `true` for the default, or `false` for nothing. Default: the element that
had focus when it opened, else the trigger.

parts.name: Portal
parts.description: Moves the popup to a different part of the DOM (the end of `<body>` by default). A dialog is fixed to the viewport, so a scope's `PortalHost` does not take it: it stays in the body and wears the scope's attributes.

props.description: Render the popup even while the dialog is closed (hidden).

props.description: Where to render: an element, a shadow root, or a function that returns one. Default `document.body`.

props.name: arrowPadding

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Do not follow the anchor after the first placement.

props.name: collisionAvoidance

props.name: lazyFlip
props.description:
Flip lazily: once the popup is placed, the side it settled on is the side it starts from, so it flips back only when that side no
longer fits (a list that filters while open). Base UI applies this inside its Combobox positioner only; here every positioner takes it.

props.name: adaptiveOrigin
props.description:

(`right` / `bottom`), so a size transition grows toward the anchor. Only a popup with a CSS transition is affected. Base UI turns this on
when the popup has a `Viewport` part; here every positioner takes it.

members.name: useFilteredItems
members.description: The items the root listed after filtering and limiting (groups when `items` are groups).

exports.name: AutocompleteRootActions
exports.description: `actionsRef` of an autocomplete root: close the popup, or unmount one kept mounted after closing.

exports.name: AutocompleteRootChangeEventDetails
exports.description: Why the value, the open state or the highlight changed.

exports.name: AutocompleteRootHighlightEventDetails
exports.description: What `onItemHighlighted` hears: why the highlight moved, and the event.

props.name: mode
props.description: How the list and the text relate: `list` (filtered), `both` (filtered, inline completion), `inline` (all items, inline completion), `none`.

props.name: value
props.description: The text (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The text at first (uncontrolled).

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the text changes, with why.

props.name: itemToStringValue
props.description: For object values: the text the input shows when an item is chosen (and a form submits). A `{ value, label }` object needs none.

props.name: openOnInputClick
props.description: Whether the popup opens when the input is pressed.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open (controlled).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popup is initially open (uncontrolled).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popup opens or closes, with why.

props.name: children
props.description: The combobox's parts: `Combobox.Input`, `Combobox.Portal` and the rest.

props.name: id
props.description: The id of the component (its input, or its trigger when the input is inside the popup).

props.name: form
props.description: Identifies the form that owns the hidden input; useful when the combobox is rendered outside the form.

props.name: filter
props.description: Matches an item against the query; `null` lists every item. Default: `contains` under `Intl.Collator`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to choose a different option from the popup.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must choose a value before submitting a form.

props.name: grid
props.description: Whether the items are laid out as a grid (`Combobox.Row` rows).

props.name: items
props.description: The items: a flat array or an array of groups (`{ value, items }`). With them the root filters, limits and labels the values itself.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: The items are virtualized by you: give each `Combobox.Item` its `index`.

props.name: inline
props.description: The list is rendered where you put it, with no popup.

props.name: limit
props.description: The most items listed (-1: no limit).

props.name: modal
props.description: `true`: the page is blocked and its scroll locked while the popup is open.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the string comparison. Default: the runtime's.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether the arrow keys loop through the list and back to the input (APG: the input is part of the loop).

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to the hidden input element.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Called after any animations complete when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: highlightItemOnHover
props.description: Whether moving the pointer over items highlights them. Off, CSS `:hover` and the keyboard highlight (`data-highlighted`) can differ.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: Imperative actions: `unmount()` (the popup then stays mounted after closing until it is called) and `close()`.

props.name: autoHighlight
props.description: Whether the first matching item is highlighted: `true` after the user types (kept while the query changes), `"always"` as soon as the list opens.

props.name: keepHighlight
props.description: Whether the highlight stays when the pointer leaves the list.

props.name: homeEndKeys
props.description:
Whether Home and End on the input move the highlight to the first and the last item instead of the caret (a command menu, where the list is the point and the
text is a filter). Only while the list is showing.

props.name: highlightedValue
props.description:
The value of the item to highlight (controlled from outside; `onItemHighlighted` reports every change the user makes). The highlight moves to the item whose
value equals it whenever this prop or the listed items change; `undefined` leaves the highlight to the user. A value no listed item has is ignored.

props.name: onItemHighlighted
props.description: Called when an item is highlighted or unhighlighted (`undefined` for none) with why (`keyboard`, `pointer`, `none` for code) and its index.

props.name: filteredItems
props.description: The items to list, filtered by you (see `useFilter`); the root then does not filter `items`.

props.name: submitOnItemClick
props.description: Whether choosing an item submits the owning form.

exports.name: AutocompleteRootState
exports.description: The autocomplete root's state; it has none, since the root renders no element.

props.name: children
props.description: What to show: a node, or a function of the text. Default: the text.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: Performs an action when clicked. Renders a `<button>` with the toast's `actionProps`; nothing when there is no label.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the part renders a native `<button>`; set false when `render` gives another element.

parts.name: Close
parts.description: Closes the toast when clicked. Renders a `<button>`.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the part renders a native `<button>`; set false when `render` gives another element.

parts.name: Content
parts.description: A container for the contents of a toast. Renders a `<div>`.

parts.name: Description
parts.description:
A description that describes the toast; the message when there is no title. Renders a `

`; nothing when the toast has no description and no children are given.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: A title that labels the toast. Renders an `<h2>`; nothing when the toast has no title and no children are given.

parts.name: Arrow
parts.description: Displays an element positioned against the toast anchor. Renders a `<div>`.

parts.name: Portal
parts.description: A portal element that moves the viewport (or an anchored toast) to a different part of the DOM; appended to `<body>` by default, or to the scope that contains the anchor.

props.name: children
props.description: The positioner and toast to move.

props.name: container
props.description: Render into this element instead of `document.body`.

props.name: anchor
props.description:
The element the toast points at, when the portal is not given a `Positioner toast={toast}` as a child to read it from: the toast goes
into the scope (`PortalHost`) that contains it, not the one the manager component happens to be rendered in.

props.name: className
props.description: A class for the node the portal creates.

parts.name: Positioner
parts.description: Positions the toast against the anchor. Renders a `<div>`.

props.name: anchor
props.description: An element to position the toast against. Defaults to the toast's `positionerProps.anchor`.

props.name: toast
props.description: The toast object associated with the positioner.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keep the popup against its anchor's edge while the anchor scrolls away.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the anchor the popup sits on; `inline-start` / `inline-end` follow the text direction.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment along that side.

props.name: sideOffset
props.type: number | ((data: { side: AnchoredSideRequest; align: AnchoredAlign; anchor: { width: number; height: number }; positioner: { width: number; height: number } }) => number
props.description: Gap between anchor and popup, px or a function of the placement.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description: `absolute` (default) follows the page while it scrolls; `fixed` places in the viewport.

props.name: alignOffset
props.type: number | ((data: { side: AnchoredSideRequest; align: AnchoredAlign; anchor: { width: number; height: number }; positioner: { width: number; height: number } }) => number
props.description: Shift along the anchor's edge.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: What the popup must stay inside.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Space kept from the boundary's edges.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description: Space kept between the arrow and the popup's corners.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Do not follow the anchor after the first placement.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description: Flip, shift or neither, per axis.

props.name: lazyFlip
props.description:
Flip lazily: once the popup is placed, the side it settled on is the side it starts from, so it flips back only when that side no
longer fits (a list that filters while open). Base UI applies this inside its Combobox positioner only; here every positioner takes it.

props.name: adaptiveOrigin
props.description:
Keep `--transform-origin` right while the popup resizes or morphs: a popup on the `left` or `top` side is written from its far edge
(`right` / `bottom`), so a size transition grows toward the anchor. Only a popup with a CSS transition is affected. Base UI turns this on
when the popup has a `Viewport` part; here every positioner takes it.

parts.name: Provider
parts.description: Provides a context for creating and managing toasts. Renders no element.

props.name: children
props.description: The app, including the viewport and every part that calls `useToastManager()`.

props.name: timeout
props.description: The default amount of time (in ms) before a toast is auto dismissed. A value of `0` prevents it being dismissed automatically.

props.name: limit
props.description: The maximum number of toasts that can be displayed at once. When the limit is reached, the oldest toast is marked `limited` to make room for the new one.

props.name: toastManager
props.description: A global manager for toasts to use outside of a React component.

parts.name: Root
parts.description: Groups all parts of an individual toast. Renders a `<div>`.

props.name: toast
props.description: The toast to render.

props.name: swipeDirection
props.description: Direction(s) in which the toast can be swiped to dismiss. A toast with an anchor does not swipe.

props.name: swipeThreshold
props.description: Distance (px) past which a released swipe dismisses; a function gets the element and the direction. A Kitora seam: Base UI's is fixed at 40.

parts.name: Viewport
parts.description: A container viewport for toasts. Renders a `<div>`.
